title: Gel Coat Repair Tech - Whitmire
description:
The Gel Coat Repair Technician is responsible for inspecting, repairing, and restoring gel coat surfaces on boats during and after the manufacturing process. This role ensures all fiberglass and gel-coated components meet company quality standards for appearance, durability, and finish. The technician works with various tools, materials, and finishing techniques to correct cosmetic and structural surface defects prior to final delivery.

Key Responsibilities

  • Inspect boat hulls, decks, and components for gel coat defects such as scratches, chips, cracks, air bubbles, blisters, and discoloration.
  • Perform gel coat repairs including color matching, filling, sanding, polishing, and buffing.
  • Prepare surfaces for repair by cleaning, grinding, sanding, and masking affected areas.
  • Mix and apply gel coat materials according to manufacturer specifications.
  • Use hand tools, power tools, sanders, buffers, and spray equipment safely and effectively.
  • Ensure repaired surfaces meet company quality and cosmetic standards.
  • Maintain a clean and organized work area.
  • Follow safety procedures for handling chemicals, resins, solvents, and equipment.
  • Document repairs and communicate recurring quality issues to supervisors.
  • Assist with final finishing and detailing as needed.
  • Maintain assigned Safety Training.
  • Additional duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED preferred.
  • 1–3 years of experience in gel coat repair, fiberglass repair, auto body repair, or marine finishing preferred.
  • Experience in boat manufacturing is highly preferred.
  • Detail oriented and good time management

Key Competencies

  • Knowledge of fiberglass, gel coat materials, and marine finishing processes.
  • Ability to color match gel coat finishes accurately.
  • Proficiency with sanding, polishing, and buffing techniques.
  • Ability to read and follow technical instructions and safety guidelines.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Basic math skills for mixing ratios and measurements.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to lift and carry/move up to 50 lbs and stand for extended periods.
  • Frequent needs to: climb, crawl, push, pull, lift, rotate arms at various angles, reach overhead, reach at or below shoulder level, gross and fine manipulation to operate hand and power tools, stooping, crouching, kneeling, crawling, speaking, hearing, visually inspecting work, etc.
  • Work in an environment with exposure to noise at levels not requiring ear protection, chemicals, and dust. Must be able to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including respirators, gloves, and eye protection.
  • Seasonal Temperatures may impact work environment.

description:

The Opportunity

You’re a natural leader who knows that great claims handling is equal parts expertise, empathy, and good judgment. As Director, you will operate at both a strategic and operational level, balancing senior leadership responsibilities with day-to-day oversight to ensure claims practices align with organizational practices, objectives and regulatory requirements. AMA is more than a workplace; it’s a family. Together, we help protect the things that matter most to our more than one-million members - everything from roadside safety to retail savings, food security to childhood well-being. And with operations that span automotive, registries, travel, insurance and more, the opportunities to grow with us are almost limitless!

Strategy, Transformation & Stakeholder Alignment

title: Lead Product GRC Subject Matter Expert
description:
At Vanta, our mission is to help businesses earn and prove trust. We believe that security should be monitored and verified continuously, and we empower companies to practice better security and prove it with ease. Vanta has a kind and talented team, and while some have prior security experience, many have been successful at Vanta without it.

Vanta for Government (V4G) is how we bring that mission to the public sector. As federal compliance undergoes its biggest shift in a decade — FedRAMP 20x, machine-readable authorization, OSCAL — we're building the platform that turns federal frameworks into automated, continuously monitored product experiences. The GRC Subject Matter Experts on this team are the people who make that possible.

As Vanta's Lead GRC Subject Matter Expert for V4G, you'll own federal compliance content used by every customer pursuing or maintaining federal authorization on our platform. This is an interpretation-and-authoring role, not a compliance program administration role: your job is to interpret underlying control requirements, identify where FedRAMP modifies or constrains the NIST framework, and translate those interpretations into precise, technically testable guidance that engineering can build and customers can act on. The content you write ships as product — a five-person startup and a Fortune 100 CSP both receive it — so calibrating depth, precision, and universality is the core craft.

You'll join Vanta's Security organization, which directly influences product development, facilitates the creation of automated GRC solutions for customers, and provides expert advisory services across the company.

What you’ll do as a V4G GRC SME at Vanta:

  • Build and own federal compliance frameworks — Lead the creation, enhancement, and lifecycle management of controls, evidence requirements, and implementation guidance for FedRAMP (Low/Moderate/High), NIST SP 800-53, NIST SP 800-171, CMMC, DFARS, and StateRAMP. Author clear control rationales, acceptance criteria, and customer-facing guidance shipped as out-of-the-box product content.

  • Interpret controls at the mechanics level — Work fluently with 800-53A assessment procedures and 800-53B baselines; resolve organization-defined parameters and FedRAMP's constraints on them; decompose controls into distinct technical obligations; correctly resolve inherited, shared, and customer-owned responsibilities within a customer responsibility matrix; and anchor evidence expectations in authoritative artifacts (PPSM, STIG and CIS hardening standards and their scan outputs across operating systems, databases, network devices, and endpoints).

  • Author automated tests & continuous monitoring — Translate controls and infrastructure context (AWS GovCloud, Azure Government, GCP, SaaS, endpoints, CI/CD) into spec-level automated tests and detectors. Define test logic, data sources, edge cases, and — critically — failure conditions: how unapproved items, exceptions, missing data, and unevaluated resources affect a result. Pair with Engineering to implement and maintain detectors with versioned framework mappings.

  • Lead V4G's machine-readable future — Shape how Vanta's federal content is architected for OSCAL and FedRAMP 20x: machine-readable SSPs, config-as-compliance, and continuous authorization workflows.

  • Design crosswalks and mappings — Maintain bidirectional crosswalks across federal frameworks (800-53 ↔ 800-171 ↔ CMMC ↔ StateRAMP) with canonical control IDs, mapping confidence, and traceability to source authority.

  • Act as a product advisor across discovery & design — Partner with the V4G PM and Design on feature discovery, review UI/UX for control, evidence, and authorization workflows, and author PRDs and acceptance criteria grounded in agency, auditor, and 3PAO needs.

  • Enable AI-assisted compliance — Partner with Engineering/ML to design LLM-powered guidance and automation for federal workflows. Translate SME knowledge into machine-readable specs, define gold-standard evaluation sets, and implement quality and safety guardrails.

  • Synthesize feedback loops — Analyze input from customers, agencies, 3PAOs, and internal teams to identify content gaps and ship iterative updates quickly and safely.

  • Raise the bar — Mentor and calibrate other SMEs, set content quality standards for the federal portfolio, and set framework strategy that others execute against.

How to be successful in this role:

  • Experience — 8–10+ years in GRC and/or Information Security with hands-on federal compliance work: building or maintaining FedRAMP programs on the CSP side, authoring SSPs and supporting artifacts, and running continuous monitoring. DoD impact-level (IL4/IL5) or CMMC experience is a strong plus. Note: this is a builder role — candidates whose federal experience is primarily assessment (3PAO) or compliance program coordination will find the day-to-day is materially different from that work.

  • Federal interpretation depth — Demonstrated fluency with the NIST 800-53/FedRAMP relationship, 800-53A/B, organization-defined parameters, control inheritance vs. non-applicability, customer responsibility matrices, PPSM, and STIG/CIS benchmarks.

  • OSCAL & FedRAMP 20x — Working familiarity with OSCAL or other machine-readable compliance approaches, and an informed point of view on where federal authorization is heading.

  • Test-design rigor — Ability to turn a control into a functional test with defined pass and failure conditions, evidence sufficiency criteria, and coverage across relevant system components.

  • Product mindset — Ability to translate requirements into productizable capabilities usable by organizations of every size; comfort with experimentation and data-driven prioritization.

  • Technical & automation (AI-augmented) — Active, current use of AI in GRC work: AI pair-programming tools to accelerate specs, mappings, and test logic; lightweight automations across Sheets/Airtable, APIs, and webhooks; AI-augmented workflows (LLM-assisted control guidance, cross-framework mapping, evidence triage) with measured outcomes; and safe-use patterns for prompts and agents.

  • Analytical & detail-oriented — Precise control wording, mapping accuracy, and evidence specificity; comfortable in spreadsheets and large datasets.

  • Communication & collaboration — Excellent written and verbal skills; effective with engineers, designers, GTM teams, agencies, 3PAOs, and customers.

  • Self-motivated and independent — Operates autonomously at Lead level, setting direction rather than awaiting it.

  • Nice-to-have — StateRAMP, CNSSI 1253/ICD 503, GovCloud or IL-environment architecture experience, or prior product/content roles at a GRC platform.

  • Certifications (preferred, not required) — One or more of: CISSP-ISSEP, CISA, FedRAMP 3PAO assessor credentials (CCP/CCA), CISM, or equivalent experience.

  • Open to using AI to amplify their skills and strengthen their work - demonstrating curiosity, a willingness to learn, and sound judgment in applying AI responsibly to improve efficiency and impact.

title: Data Science and Analytics Specialist
description:
ABOUT US | HR&A Advisors, Inc. (HR&A) is an employee-owned company advising public, private, non-profit, and philanthropic clients on how to increase opportunity and advance quality of life in cities.

We believe in creating vital places, building equitable and resilient communities, and improving people’s lives.

From Brooklyn to London, Medellin to Hong Kong, we have guided hundreds of clients in transforming real estate and economic development concepts, and public infrastructure, first into actionable plans and then into job-producing, community-strengthening assets.

Our clients include real estate owners and investors, hospitals and universities, cultural institutions and philanthropies, community development organizations, and governments.

HR&A has offices in Atlanta, Dallas, Los Angeles, New York, Raleigh, Washington D.C. and the Bay Area. We come from diverse backgrounds, have a breadth of lived experience, and share a passion for cities. We are former city officials, executive directors, planners, lawyers, architects, and economists.

Hear more about the HR&A experience from our staff.

Learn more about careers at HR&A on our website here.

THE OPPORTUNITY | HR&A Labs is a rapidly growing internal team that works closely with project teams across all of our business lines to prototype products, serve data science requests, and increase the quality and efficiency of our work. Over the past four years, HR&A Labs has developed dashboards, products, and actionable data analysis to state and local governments to push forward housing access, broadband adoption, and data transparency.

This position will primarily support the design and implementation of internal data tools and be deployed onto projects to help provide data science and analytics expertise across a wide set of business lines.

THE ROLE | HR&A Labs is seeking a Data Science and Analytics Specialist to support the rapid growth of our digital services offerings. This role is based in our New York office. This role is for early-career professionals with roughly 2-4 years of experience who want to grow into owning the substance of client and internal deliverables. As a Data Science and Analytics Specialist, you will contribute to and increasingly drive complex data analytics, visualization, and web development work, with high impact across numerous projects and the opportunity to build both our clients' capacities and your own skills quickly.

EXPERIENCE REQUIRED | You will support the rapid growth of our digital service offerings by conducting data and geospatial analysis, developing visualizations, building interactive tools and dashboards, and developing methodologies for key economic indicators. Day-to-day work includes procuring and analyzing large datasets, building and maintaining data systems and tools, and contributing to fast-moving project teams. You'll start by driving discrete pieces of the work and grow into leading workstreams as you demonstrate ownership.

  • 2-4 years of relevant professional experience, or a strong portfolio that demonstrates equivalent capability in analytics and product thinking

  • Proficiency in Python, including geospatial analysis and packages (e.g., GeoPandas, Shapely)

  • Demonstrated ability to work with census data, PUMS, and other economic and demographic datasets

  • Proficiency cleaning, manipulating, and merging public, proprietary, and internal datasets for analysis

  • Fluency with LLMs and other AI tools as part of a daily workflow, paired with the judgment to independently verify data and AI outputs and catch when they are wrong

  • Clear written and verbal communication, including the ability to translate technical analysis into something a non-technical client can read and act on

  • Evidence of self-directed drive: something you built, shipped, or contributed to that nobody assigned you (a side project, a tool, an open-source contribution)

  • Ability to manage your own deadlines across multiple workstreams and escalate early when something is at risk

  • Bachelor’s degree (master’s preferred) with a focus on data science/analytics, geographic information science/analytics, urban planning/design/data, regional science/analytics, architecture, economics, business, public policy, real estate, or other related fields

Preferred:

  • Experience building web-based tools and dashboards using publicly available APIs

  • Experience with front-end development (React/Next.js) and/or back-end services (FastAPI)

  • Experience with spatial data infrastructure (PostGIS, vector tiles) or analytical databases (DuckDB)

  • Experience conducting geospatial, vicinity/buffer, site suitability, socio-economic, and demographic analysis

  • Experience in product design, rapid prototyping (including with generative AI tools), and wireframing

HYBRID WORK POLICY | HR&A fosters a collaborative and flexible work environment through our hybrid work policy. Employees work from the office at least three days a week, which allows individuals the freedom to balance their professional and personal lives while maintaining a strong connection to their teams.

COMPENSATION | The base salary range for this position is $83,200 to $98,571, plus the opportunity for a discretionary year-end bonus. Where an offer falls inside this pay range is dependent on experience. We offer competitive compensation packages, based on qualifications and experience. We are an employee-owned company, meaning you will have the opportunity to benefit from the firm’s growth over time through participation in our Employee Stock Ownership Plan. Each year, the firm will contribute funds to this long-term wealth-building account and may make contributions to other retirement accounts. We also provide a comprehensive benefits package that goes well beyond coverage of 90-95% of healthcare premiums, including dental and vision coverage.

HOW TO APPLY | HR&A is committed to attracting and retaining a talented, diverse, competitive team of professionals dedicated to solving the challenges of urban life. Women, people of color, members of the LGBTQ community, individuals with disabilities, and veterans are strongly encouraged to apply.

title: Senior Presales, System Engineer

Senior Presales, System Engineer

This role has been designated as ‘Remote/Teleworker’, which means you will primarily work from home.

Who We Are:

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. Job Description:

About This Position

In this customer focused Senior Presales Engineering (SE) role you will, as part of the HPE sales team, play an important role in driving the technical sales activities for a selected set of our Tier 2 Service Provider customers in Italy.

HPE Senior Presales Engineers have a deep technical knowledge, including strong hands-on experience with HPE's products + services as well as good insights into competitor's products and solutions. The SE serves as the technical expertise for the regional sales efforts, creating and proposing solutions - with the full range of HPE products and solutions at your disposal - that fits the customer’s requirements and addresses the customer’s needs.

For this role the ideal candidate comes with solid experience in working with Service Provider networks, around +8 yeswars, has a knowledge of HPE Networking’s products and solutions as well as competitor’s products and services. Equally important is the ability to develop trusted and long-lasting relationships with our key customer technical decision makers through an in-depth understanding of the customer’s needs, priorities, organizational structure, and decision process.

Beyond the classical networking and network product know-how, the topics of virtualization and automation are becoming an important criteria in many customer tenders and discussions. Therefore, Sales Engineers should be able to lead the discussion also in this area with presentations, demos, etc.

You will be part of a great local team with lots of interaction with the SE peers, Account Managers, and other parts of the organization.

Responsibilities:

  • Drive the technical sales activities which includes working closely with the customers to fully understand customer requirements, and from there:
  • Propose solutions, guide customers on how HPE products and solutions can solve the customer challenges and address their business needs.
  • Engage and influence customer technology strategies through showcasing HPE innovative technologies through technical sales presentations, whiteboarding sessions, customer technology events, product demonstrations and evaluations and proof of concepts.
  • Build, develop, and maintain strong, trusted, professional relationships with customer technical decision-makers and partner community.
  • Lead the technical responses for RFP/RFQ and build BoMs for relevant sales opportunities. Capture new customer or industry requirements and trends and feed this into the business units.
  • Continuously learn and stay ahead of the industry and competitive solutions, products, and services.
  • Enjoy the personal growth career opportunity that comes from exposure to the latest technological innovations and apply these capabilities to address the real-world challenges of our customers.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • +8 years of experience in Sales/Presales.
  • Fluent in English.
  • Strong experience in working with Service Provider networks in a technical/pre-sales role as a Sales/Systems Engineer and/or Network architecture roles.
  • Expert level knowledge in Routing technologies, routing protocols including MPLS, SR etc is a MUST, as well as experience in some of the following areas: Automation, Cloud/DC, Security, Network Virtualization.
  • Proven technical capability, ability to learn quickly, and apply skills in new areas as well as being able to explain complex matters in a structured and easy to understand way.
  • Knowledge and/or strong interest in network automation and network virtualization is desired.
  • Knowledge in automation using e.g. Python, Ansible, Netconf YANG, JSON, Openconfig is desirable.
  • Knowledge in Service Provider security is a plus.
  • Good understanding of Service Provider market trends and emerging use cases.
  • Knowledge of HPE’s products and solutions is desirable.
  • Knowledge of HPE competitor's products and services
  • The candidate must have strong written, oral and communication/presentation skills with the ability to discuss highly technical concepts to a variety of audiences including all levels of technical decision-makers.
  • Like working with people, discussing and explaining complex details in an easy-to-understand way.
  • Positive attitude, a desire to learn new technologies and the ability to handle interruptions in a challenging and high pace environment.
  • Ability to keep many plates spinning in parallel and work well under pressure.
  • Be self-motivated and a strong Team player while being able to work independently with minimum supervision.
  • Bachelor's and/or master’s degree in engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, and related field or equivalent experience.
  • Industry certifications such as JNCIA, JNCIS, JNCIP, JNCIE and/or CISSP, CCIE certificates are beneficial.

What We Can Offer You:

Health & Wellbeing

We strive to provide our team members and their loved ones with a comprehensive suite of benefits that supports their physical, financial and emotional wellbeing.

Personal & Professional Development

We also invest in your career because the better you are, the better we all are. We have specific programs catered to helping you reach any career goals you have — whether you want to become a knowledge expert in your field or apply your skills to another division.

Unconditional Inclusion

We are unconditionally inclusive in the way we work and celebrate individual uniqueness. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good.

description:

Employment Type: FULL_TIME

Position Summary

Odyssey Systems has an exciting new opportunity for a Security Visitor Control Monitor supporting the Space Systems Command (SSC) System Delta 85 (SYD 85) in the United States Space Force which consists of ground-based radars and command and control systems. The System Delta delivers integrated Space Domain Awareness (SDA), missile warning and tracking, Command, Control, and Communication (C3), Battle Management, and Space Intelligence capabilities for the USSF and joint warfighters. As the Visitor Control Monitor, you will have the opportunity to grow and develop while being a cornerstone of the facilities security team.

Responsibilities

The Contractor shall provide the following security support services for SSC SYD 85/S4 operations on Peterson SFB:

  • Perform entry and access controls 12 hours/day, 5 days/week for Building 1840, Peterson AFB. Building 1840 contains one entry point requiring such controls.
  • The contractor shall continually monitor all persons entering and leaving Building 1840 to ensure that only authorized persons are permitted entry and that accountable U.S. Government equipment and classified media is not transported out of the building without proper authorization and monitor vehicles for suspicious activities.
  • Ingress controls shall include employee badge checks, identification and control of visitors (using an SYD 85 controlled database) and issuance of visitor badges, an examination of any suspicious packages/objects carried into the building, continuous monitoring of alarm panels and re-setting alarms as required, coordination with SYD security personnel on any unusual situation or problem, and notification of emergency conditions to the Installation Security Forces and/or Fire Department.
  • Egress controls shall include collection of issued visitor badges, an observation of items/objects being carried by persons leaving the building and, if computer hardware or test equipment is being carried, the individual shall be asked to produce a hand receipt or other written authorization for removal of the item from the building. If no written authorization can be produced, an SYD security person shall be summoned immediately.
  • Contractor personnel shall comply with the applicable portions of the building 1840 Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) written by SYD 85 Security. A copy of this SOP shall be maintained at each entry control desk.
  • Contractor personnel shall assist SYD 85 Security in conducting Random Anti-terrorism Measures (random security checks in and around the building), Building emergency evacuations, and other documentation related to control of entry at Building 1840. The contractors will assist SYD 85 Security with any other duties that the Commander, the Chief of Security, or the members of the security staff direct to provide for the safety and security of U.S. Government resources and personnel.
  • Ensure administrative and physical measures are in place to mitigate vulnerabilities that jeopardize human life and physical property.
  • Escort personnel
  • Assistances the Prime Facility Manager, Commander, the Chief of Security, or the members of the security staff direct to provide for the safety and security of U.S. Government resources and personnel.

Qualifications

Citizenship: Must be a US citizen

Minimum Required Qualifications

Clearance: Must have and be able to maintain a Secret level clearance Education: High School DiplomaYears of Experience: 4 years of security experience, 2 years in DoD.

Preferred Qualifications

Clearance: Top SecretEducation: Some college and/or Technical TrainingAdditional Experience: Military background

Technical Skills

• Knowledge of Operational Security (OPSEC) and Information Security (INFOSEC) principles as they apply to Department of War (DoW) and Space Force missions.• Knowledge of counter-surveillance indicators and the basic principles of identifying "insider threat" behaviors within a restricted facility.• Skill in utilizing integrated security software, automated visitor management systems (VMS), and digital logging protocols.• Ability to rapidly synthesize data from visual observations, alarm systems, and databases to make informed security decisions under pressure.

Interpersonal Skills

• Knowledge of military etiquette, rank structure, and the organizational hierarchy of Space Systems Command (SSC) to properly interact with personnel.• Skill in conflict de-escalation and professional interpersonal communication when enforcing facility restrictions or denying property removal.• Skill in delivering firm but courteous customer service while processing visitors and managing expectations at the entry control point.• Ability to communicate technical security requirements clearly and concisely to diverse audiences, including senior military officers and civilian contractors.• Ability to maintain a professional demeanor, sustained mental alertness, and high-level vigilance throughout the duration of the work shift.

Additional Information

Location: Peterson SFB, Building 1840 in Colorado Springs, CO

Travel: Travel may be required (approx 0-5%)

description:

Join S&C to make an impact on tomorrow’s energy challenges and become an employee-owner!

Hours

Compensation

At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, and we are committed to transparency in our pay practices. The estimated annual base salary range for this position is $49,040 - $61,300. Individual pay within this salary range is determined by several compensable factors, including performance, knowledge, job-related skills and experience, and relevant education or training. This role is also eligible for S&C’s annual incentive plan (AIP), subject to eligibility criteria.

Join Our Team as a Security Officer!

S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to coordinate our security function. As a Security Officer, you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team. Officers perform duties in three main categories, including patrolling the S&C Ridge Boulevard Industrial Campus facility, working in the Global Security Operations Center (GSOC), and operating the security gatehouses.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Utilize strong, written communication skills by creating clear and accurate incident and field activity reports in a timely manner.
  • Conduct and document events/ investigations with close attention to detail; gather and summarize statements and facts for records.
  • Perform routine and scheduled patrols of the S&C Campus to: regulate traffic and parking, ensure team member safety, respond to emergencies/incidents.
  • Act as first responders to critical and emergent situations including: medical emergencies, fires, hazardous material releases/spills, unauthorized personnel on campus, confined space rescues, severe weather, and building evacuations.
  • Certify and maintain required certification in the use of self-contained breathing apparatus and/or respirators.
  • Monitor fire, building supervisory, high-voltage supply, intrusion alarm, and closed-circuit video systems while assigned to the Global Security Operations Center (GSOC).
  • Monitor entry/exit and access to S&C Campus, with attention to detail for guiding team members, vehicles, visitors, and contractors. Maintain accurate logs and records of all commercial-related entrants.
  • Issue temporary identification badges and parking permits to authorized individuals.
  • Coordinate logistics of commercial deliveries and shipments from the GSOC.
  • Operate communication systems by serving as radio dispatchers and telephone switchboard operators during off-hours.
  • Directly identifying and addressing safety, trespassing and workplace violence concerns, which may include, but is not limited to, the detaining of threatening individuals for police resolution.
  • Safely remove unauthorized individuals from the campus using various de-escalation techniques.
  • Maintaining licensing and certifications for essential training and equipment necessary to perform job duties. (PERC, FOID, DL)
  • Maintain regular and punctual attendance.
  • Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required.
  • Communicate effectively and respectfully with others.
  • Drive a car or other vehicle.
  • Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
  • Other responsibilities as assigned.

What you’ll Need To Succeed:

  • High School diploma or acceptable General Educational Development (GED), some college preferred.
  • Illinois Driver’s License and Illinois Firearms Owner’s Identification Card.
  • Good verbal and written communication skills; proficiency with personal computers.
  • State of Illinois Security Officer 40-Hour Training Program for armed security
  • A Permanent Employee Registration Card (PERC) and ability to successfully obtain the Firearm Authorization Card (FAC) issued from the State of Illinois, Department of Financial and Professional Regulation.
  • 4 years of security or related background. Industrial security, law enforcement, or military experience preferred.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills
  • Strong computer and technological skills
  • Conflict resolution skills
  • De-escalation and high stress management skills
  • Understanding laws and regulations pertaining to armed security work
  • Understanding signals of distress or impairment in others

Preferred:

  • Associates Degree in Security, Criminal Justice, Law Enforcement, or related field.
  • Any advanced National Incident Management System (NIMS) training.
  • Handcuffing certification.
  • De-escalation training i.e., Crisis Prevention Institute (CPI) or Crisis Intervention (CIT) Training certifications

Major Physical Demands:

  • Frequently required to stand and perform tasks for 2-4 hours at a time approximately [5] days per work week.
  • Frequently required to remain in a stationary position and perform desk-based for 2-4 hours at a time approximately [5] days per work week.
  • Frequently required to walk moderate distances up to [1-2 miles on campus while patrolling] [frequency – e.g., multiple times each day]
  • Occasionally required to solo lift and/or carry items ranging in weight from 5 to 40 lb, and team lift and carry items or other team members to safety, exercising sound judgment to employ manual handling or machine lifts where required and risk assessments, if appropriate.
  • Occasionally required to position self to perform tasks involving but not limited to reaching, twisting, rotating, and pushing/pulling.
  • Occasionally required to use hand-eye coordination to control both hands and arms for a full range of motion to operate equipment/machinery/power tools/office productivity equipment.
  • Frequently ascending or descending ladders/stairs/scaffolding/ramps/poles.
  • Frequently required to observe details at close range, including depth perception, peripheral vision, and the ability to differentiate between colors.
  • Continuously required to talk and hear in person and by phone/conference calls.
  • Frequently required to travel (up to 10%) and work extended hours when necessary.

title: Senior Solutions Architect, WWPS ISV
description:
Application deadline: Aug 17, 2026

Do you like helping customers implement innovative cloud computing solutions and solve technical problems? Would you like to do this using the latest cloud computing technologies? Do you have a knack for helping groups understand application architectures and integration approaches, and the consultative skills to launch a project on a trajectory to success?

Are you familiar with security best practices for applications, servers, and networks? Do you want to be part of the business development team helping to establish Amazon Web Services (AWS) as a forefront technology platform? Would you like to be part of a sales group, but have your opinion valued as a technical resource as part of planning and strategies?

Amazon Web Services is looking for a highly motivated Solutions Architect to help accelerate our growing ISV Partner business as part of the World-Wide Public-Sector practice. You will be focused on ISV partners in the Enterprise resource planning (ERP) and Human capital management (HCM) space. As a Solutions Architect within AWS, you will have the opportunity to help shape and deliver on a strategy to build broad use of Amazon's utility computing web services (e.g., AWS EC2, AWS S3, AWS RDS, and AWS CloudFront) directly with customers and our ecosystem of system integrators and solution providers. Your broad responsibilities will include: owning the technical engagement and ultimate success around specific implementation projects; defining implementation architectures, responding to RFPs, developing a deep expertise in the AWS technologies as well as broad know-how around how applications and services are constructed using the AWS platform; and being a subject matter expert on security as it relates to customer applications and services.

As a Solutions Architect on our team, you will provide exceptional technical design and take an exceptional approach with our customers while partnering with a world class sales and business development team. You will help capture and share best-practice knowledge amongst the AWS solution architect community. You will gain the opportunity to learn from, collaborate with, and educate some of the brightest technical minds in the industry today across the breadth of enterprise architecture.

Here at AWS, we embrace our differences. We are committed to furthering our culture of inclusion. We have ten employee-led affinity groups, reaching 40,000 employees in over 190 chapters globally. We have innovative benefit offerings, and we host annual and ongoing learning experiences. Amazon’s culture of inclusion is reinforced within our 14 Leadership Principles, which remind team members to seek diverse perspectives, learn and be curious, and earn trust.

Our team also puts a high value on work-life balance. Striking a healthy balance between your personal and professional life is crucial to your happiness and success here, which is why we aren’t focused on how many hours you spend at work or online. Instead, we’re happy to offer a flexible schedule so you can have a more productive and well-balanced life—both in and outside of work.

Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects based on what will help each team member develop into a better-rounded professional and enable them to take on more complex tasks in the future.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen.


Key job responsibilities
* Helping our customers to design and create cloud computing architectures
* Our company credo: “Work hard. Have fun. Make history.” It’s critical to love what you do and take pride in your value proposition to our customers.
* Deep-dive technical discussions around design and a deep curiosity to always keep your technical skills current while maintaining a pulse on industry trends.
With experience in the following key areas:
* Lead complex, multi-service architecture designs workloads on AWS, driving end-to-end technical strategy for public sector customers
* Develop and deliver thought leadership content (blogs, whitepapers, reference architectures) specific to Databricks/Data & AI on AWS
* Mentor junior SAs and contribute to organizational scaling through reusable artifacts and best practices
* Identify and drive product feature requests (PFRs) based on customer feedback to influence AWS service roadmap
* Ability to travel 30%

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

title: Cloud Engineer
description:
Serves as a Cybersecurity Cloud Engineer and AWS cloud expert for pre-production efforts/activities. Ensures the architecture and design of cloud-hosted IT systems are secure and meet Department requirements; reviews cloud security policy and provides recommendations for improvement to enhance the security posture within the cloud as well as the ability to meet protection, detection, monitoring and response requirements for systems and data; applies knowledge of current advances in cloud security engineering and cloud security threats to support the deployment of programs and applications; provides input to programs throughout the process of deployment to ensure systems meet Department compliance requirements; and provides guidance to assessment staff in the performance of Cybersecurity Vulnerability Assessments as related to cloud hosting environments. On this task order, works alongside the program's designated cloud lead to manage and stand up the AWS environments and accounts, and applies working knowledge of AWS GovCloud and Department environment requirements.

*This position is contingent upon contract award.*

Responsibilities:

  • Manage and set up the AWS environments and accounts, working alongside the program's designated cloud lead.
  • Apply AWS GovCloud expertise and Department environment requirements to the design, provisioning, and hardening of all cloud accounts and landing zones.
  • Scale the current prototype environment, or an equivalent AWS environment, into a full pre-production environment supporting development, test, and integration.
  • Engineer the environment to support a relational database, a modern software language (i.e., Java), cloud native capability, Zero Trust (ZT)/ICAM, API integration, a modern UI/UX, and CI/CD implementation.
  • Implement the pre-production architecture necessary to support parallel production.
  • Ensure the architecture and design of cloud-hosted IT systems are secure and meet Department requirements; review cloud security policy and recommend improvements to the cloud security posture.
  • Support protection, detection, monitoring, and response requirements for systems and data hosted in the cloud environment.
  • Provide guidance to assessment staff in the performance of Cybersecurity Vulnerability Assessments related to the cloud hosting environment.
  • Support achievement of IATT-C and ATO accreditations in the cloud environment and implementation of RMF controls.
  • Support container orchestration, microservices deployment, automated environment provisioning, and infrastructure as code (IaC) in AWS.
  • Contribute cloud architecture content to EA artifacts and design diagrams.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

Years of Experience: 5 Years

Education Level: None. Desired BS in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, IT, or closely related discipline, or equivalent additional relevant experience.

Clearance Requirements: Secret. Must possess IT-II Non-Critical Sensitive security clearance or Tier 3 (T3) at time of proposal submission.

Certification Requirements: None. AWS Solutions Architect – Associate and/or CISSP desired.

Any other work-related qualifications needed for the role:

  • Must be specifically an AWS cloud engineer/expert — general multi-cloud experience alone does not satisfy this requirement.
  • Demonstrated familiarity with AWS GovCloud and Department environment requirements.
  • Extensive knowledge of FedRAMP assessment methodology.
  • Experience working with OCI.
  • Experience working with enterprise DoD IT.
  • Experience standing up and administering cloud accounts, organizations, IAM boundaries, and network segmentation in a regulated Government environment.
  • Extensive experience working on highly complex IT systems. Resume must demonstrate experience working legacy system upgrades, modernization, legacy system transition, data migration and/or system analysis and design. Priority given to personnel with demonstrated experience performing functional and technical solutions decomposition that enables solutions analysis and design and demonstrated experience implementing solutions with respect to modern database design and modern software languages within the federal Government, specifically within the DoD. AI/ML experience is preferred.
  • Travel to on-site meetings in Columbus, OH (Onsite once per month (average) up to 3 days.)

title: Chief Information Security Officer
description:
Chief Information Security Officer

Location: Cleveland, OH, US

Employment Type: FULL_TIME

Overview

The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) is responsible for establishing, executing, and continuously evolving the enterprise cybersecurity and information risk management strategy. The CISO provides executive leadership for the protection of customer, policyholder, employee, and corporate information assets while enabling business growth, innovation, digital transformation, and regulatory compliance.

The CISO serves as a trusted advisor to executive leadership and the Board of Directors, ensuring cybersecurity risks are effectively identified, managed, communicated, and aligned with the organization's strategic objectives. The role oversees enterprise security governance, cyber defense, privacy collaboration, operational resilience, and regulatory readiness across all business units.

Responsibilities

  • Develop a risk-based cybersecurity strategy, roadmap, and governance framework aligned with business objectives, informed by ongoing assessments of cybersecurity maturity, control effectiveness, and organizational capabilities.
  • Continuously assess and optimize the cybersecurity organization's structure, capabilities, and resource allocation to address evolving business, technology, regulatory, and threat landscape requirements
  • Oversee the planning, execution, and performance tracking of the enterprise cybersecurity portfolio, ensuring strategic initiatives are delivered on time, within budget, and aligned with organizational risk management and business objectives.
  • Build, scale, and mature enterprise security operations capabilities, including security monitoring, threat intelligence, threat detection, incident response, vulnerability management, cyber resilience, and recovery readiness to effectively identify, contain, and mitigate cyber threats.
  • Lead the organization's response to cybersecurity incidents, ensuring effective containment, recovery, stakeholder communication, and continuous improvement.
  • Partner with business and technology leaders to identify, assess, and remediate security risks across infrastructure, applications, cloud environments, and third-party relationships.
  • Advise executive leadership and the Board on cybersecurity risks, emerging threats, and strategic security investments.
  • Promote a culture of security awareness, accountability, and regulatory compliance across the organization.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, Cybersecurity, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum 15 years of progressive information security and technology leadership experience.
  • Minimum 8 years of executive-level cybersecurity leadership experience.
  • Proven success leading and maturing security operations functions, including incident response, threat management, security monitoring, and cyber resilience capabilities.
  • Hands-on experience managing significant cybersecurity incidents and coordinating enterprise-wide response and recovery efforts.
  • Deep understanding of enterprise security architecture, cloud security, identity and access management, application security, data protection, and regulatory compliance frameworks.
  • Strong executive presence with the ability to communicate complex security risks and business impacts to senior leadership and boards.
  • Experience managing security budgets, organizational strategy, and high-performing cybersecurity teams.

Preferred:

  • Professional certifications such as: CISSP, CISM, CISA, CRISC, CCSP

title: Clinical Pharmacologist
description:
Position
You will play a critical role in ensuring the safe and effective use of medications for all patients at AHI. The role involves reviewing medication appropriateness, monitoring drug interactions, detecting and analyzing adverse drug reactions, and conducting prescription audits. You will work closely with physicians and other healthcare professionals to adjust doses, monitor restricted antibiotic use, and ensure compliance with hospital policies and standards such as JCI and NABH.

Key Responsibilities
  • Conduct daily morning rounds for all in-patient department (IPD) patients and review prescriptions in wards and ICUs before dispensing.
  • Lead the prescription audit team, ensuring thorough reviews and compliance with hospital policies.
  • Collaborate with doctors to adjust doses for patients with abnormal pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, particularly in cases of renal and hepatic impairment.
  • Monitor restricted antibiotic use and coordinate with the infection control officer for the antibiotic stewardship program.
  • Prevent, anticipate, and investigate potential drug interactions and adverse drug reactions, presenting monthly reports on these issues to the quality department.
  • Monitor and implement the hospital’s narcotic policy, ensuring compliance.
  • Regularly check and verify the contents of crash carts and disaster kits.
  • Oversee blood sugar monitoring for all IPD patients and ensure timely incident reporting for any major incidents.
  • Provide daily reports on medication errors, adverse drug reactions, incomplete prescriptions, dispensing errors, and patient counseling sessions.
  • Ensure proper drug information is provided to both doctors and patients, with detailed counseling during patient discharge.
  • Conduct training sessions for ward and ICU pharmacists and nurses, keeping them up to date with clinical practices.
  • Coordinate and organize meetings for the Therapeutic Committee, maintain minutes, and follow up on action items.
  • Regularly update the hospital’s drug formulary, ensuring compliance with storage regulations and monitor medication expiry dates.
  • Maintain room and refrigerator temperatures according to FDA regulations.
  • Monitor medication appropriateness, conducting audits, and ensuring safe and effective drug use according to JCI and NABH standards.
Qualifications
  • Either Masters or Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharma D) is required
  • Minimum 2 years experience.

About Asian Heart Institute
Asian Heart Institute is India's #1 cardiac hospital dedicated to incorporating the latest technological advances and ethical practices to provide quality heart care at reasonable costs. As a JCI, NABH, and ISO-accredited hospital with a staggering success rate of 99.83% in bypass surgeries and an overall 99.4% in cardiac surgeries, we are considered among the best globally.

Our foundation rests firmly on four core pillars: Ethics, Experience, Excellence, and Expertise. At the heart of our approach is a steadfast commitment to integrity and ethical practices, ensuring that every patient is treated with the highest level of respect and care. We take pride in our team of renowned experts, each contributing years of specialized experience and skill, which is pivotal in driving our pursuit of excellence. Our focus on expertise is not just about having the best professionals on board, but also about fostering continuous learning and staying ahead in our field.

title: Senior Mechanical Engineer - Wire Harness Design
description:
Primary Function of Position

The Systems Mechanical Engineering team is responsible for the development of multiport da Vinci Surgical Systems from product concept through market launch and initial product stabilization.

The Mechanical Engineer will design medical capital equipment components for volume manufacturing processes. They are expected to use creativity and analytical skills to develop, document, and verify new mechanical wiring harness designs. They will interface with multiple functions including, but not limited to, electrical engineering, systems engineering, manufacturing, procurement, supplier engineering, quality, and regulatory.

The Mechanical Engineer, Wiring Harness Design is expected to use first-principles design methodology and analytical skills to conceptualize, develop, and verify new mechanical wiring harness designs. The Mechanical Engineer must utilize creativity and sound engineering judgment in the design of medical capital equipment components for volume manufacturing processes. They are responsible for key system components and will interface with suppliers and manufacturing to build high-quality hardware prototypes and productize new designs. They will be expected to excel in a focused, high-energy, collaborative work environment with a team of talented engineers. The Mechanical Engineer should be capable of making sound decisions when faced with time constraints and ambiguous or incomplete information typical of research and development.

This role can be up-leveled to align with candidates with significantly more relevant work experience.

Roles & Responsibilities

  • Working with mechanical engineering and electrical engineering to design the interfacing cabling and wiring harness design
  • Author and release harness design documentation including: drawings, schematics, routing diagrams, etc.
  • Perform and review electrical analysis including wire sizing, voltage drop, shield grounding, and derating
  • Working within multi-disciplinary teams to define requirements for new and current designs
  • Designing for manufacturability, reliability, serviceability, and cost
  • Selecting and managing vendors in the prototype phase
  • Collaborating with manufacturing to create product assembly tooling, fixtures, and instructions
  • Developing and performing component verification testing and product validation testing
  • Supporting production of final product by troubleshooting process and component problems
  • Providing engineering support to Manufacturing, Materials, Test Engineering, and Service to facilitate transfer of designs
  • Developing mechanical wiring harness assemblies with an appropriate FOS that is proportional to the risk associated with the specific part
  • Rapid development and iteration of full-scale prototypes of candidate architectures to satisfy requirements
  • Drive design improvements through DFM and failure analysis
  • Mentor and coach other engineers in problem solving

Required

  • Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, or similar
  • 5+ years of experience with mechanical design or machine design in a regulated industry (medical device, aerospace, spacecraft, defense, etc.)
  • Broad understanding of design controls: design inputs & outputs, risks, design verification, and change control
  • Passion for details in creating robust and reliable machines designed for mission-critical applications
  • Ability to apply knowledge of engineering materials and component selection criteria to product designs through strong concept development, design analysis, hands-on prototyping, and reliability testing skills
  • Proficiency using CAD, analysis, and finite element simulation tools to design mechanical assemblies
  • Excellent communication skills, interpersonal skills, and the ability to receive and implement performance feedback
  • Self-driven with the ability to excel in a high-energy, small, focused team environment, to maintain a strong sense of shared responsibility and shared reward, and to make work fun and interesting

Preferred

  • 2+ years of experience in electrical harness design for robotic, automotive, aerospace, spacecraft, or defense applications
  • Surgical or medical device product experience
  • Ability to elevate the group knowledge of wiring harnesses design best practice
  • Understanding of grounding, shielding, EMI/EMC principles in medical devices
  • Familiarity with IEC 60601
  • Comfortable with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, qualification, and transfer
  • Experience designing for volume manufacturing processes such as metal castings, injection molding, sheet metal stamping, compression molding, thermoforming, etc.
  • Experience with harness design tools
  • SolidWorks experience

title: Senior Field Service Technician
description:
Xylem is a Fortune 500 global water solutions company dedicated to advancing sustainable impact and empowering the people who make water work every day. As a leading water technology company with 23,000 employees operating in over 150 countries, Xylem is at the forefront of addressing the world's most critical water challenges. We invite passionate individuals to join our team, dedicated to exceeding customer expectations through innovative and sustainable solutions.

Job Summary

The Senior Field Service Technician is responsible for initiating and executing field service activities at customer sites in a safe, efficient, and professional manner. This role includes proactive troubleshooting of mechanical, electrical, and diesel equipment, performing preventative maintenance, managing parts inventory, and identifying and correcting safety issues involving company- and customer-owned equipment. The technician will work directly with customers and may support multiple systems, locations, and customers.

Who We Are Looking For

Xylem is seeking experienced, mechanically inclined professionals who are passionate about hands-on work, troubleshooting, and solving technical problems in the field. We encourage individuals with backgrounds in field service, industrial or commercial process water, electrical work, diesel, mechanical systems, fusion, or related skilled trades to apply. Candidates who enjoy working independently, interacting with customers, and diagnosing equipment issues across different systems and locations are encouraged to bring their expertise to our team.

At Xylem, we are united by a shared purpose: solving water to create a more sustainable world. If you are driven by innovation, service, and making a real impact, we invite you to bring your skills to our team as a Senior Field Service Technician.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Initiate and execute field service activities at customer sites in a safe, efficient, and professional manner.
  • Proactively troubleshoot and diagnose mechanical, electrical, diesel, and other technical equipment.
  • Perform preventative maintenance and inspections to support equipment reliability.
  • Manage parts inventory and ensure required materials are available to support field service activities.
  • Identify and correct safety issues involving company- and customer-owned equipment.
  • Communicate professionally with customers regarding equipment condition, service needs, and recommended solutions.
  • Maintain company property, tools, equipment, and vehicles in good working condition.
  • Work independently with minimal supervision while effectively managing service activities and priorities.
  • Collaborate with internal teams and customers to resolve technical issues and meet service commitments.
  • Demonstrate accountability, innovation, and empowerment while supporting a high-impact culture.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • 2–5 years of technical work experience, including industrial or commercial process water experience.
  • Electrical, mechanical, diesel, and/or fusion experience depending on business unit.
  • Previous field service, industrial maintenance, or related technical experience preferred.
  • Industry-specific licenses or certifications may be preferred.
  • Ability to obtain required customer site clearances, including TWIC, DISA, or other site-specific requirements.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a DOT Medical Card.

Skills

  • Strong technical knowledge and troubleshooting abilities.
  • Strong mechanical and electrical problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal direct supervision.
  • Strong customer service and communication skills.
  • Experience using Microsoft Office applications and smart devices.
  • Ability to synthesize technical information and communicate it clearly.
  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to use customer insights and technical information to develop solutions in new and unexpected situations.
  • Commitment to continuous professional development and staying current with industry practices.

Travel and Driving Requirements

  • Overnight travel and extended time away from home may be required.
  • This position requires operating a company vehicle. Candidates must have and maintain a valid driver’s license and a clean driving record that meets company standards.
  • Candidates must successfully complete all required driver, DOT, medical, and background screening requirements.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain company driving privileges

Compensation & Benefits

The estimated pay range for this position is $27 to $30 per hour. At Xylem we offer a competitive compensation package with a generous benefit package, including Medical, Dental, Vision plans, 401(k) with company contribution, paid time off, paid parental leave and tuition reimbursement.

Our products impact public utilities, industrial sectors, residential areas, and commercial buildings, with a commitment to providing smart metering, network technologies, and advanced analytics for water, electric, and gas utilities. Partner with us in creating a world where water challenges are met with ingenuity and dedication; where we recognize the power of inclusion and belonging in driving innovation and allowing us to compete more effectively around the world.

title: Project Manager
description:
As we create a colorful, capable and cleaner world through chemistry, we invite you to join our team to harness the power of chemistry to shape markets, redefine industries and improve lives for billions of people around the world.

CREATING ESSENTIAL CHEMISTRY THAT THE WORLD NEEDS

At Chemours, our people are redefining how the world thinks of chemistry by approaching everything we do with a commitment to delivering Trusted Chemistry that creates better lives and helps communities thrive. That begins with how we use our science, data, and unmatched technical expertise to develop market-leading products with the highest levels of performance, sustainability, and safety in the industry.

Powered by chemistry, our products are used in applications that make the products we rely on, processes, and new technologies possible. In key sectors such as clean energy, advanced electronics, high-performance computing and AI, climate friendly cooling, and high-quality paints and coatings for homes and industrial infrastructure---sustainable solutions and more modern living depend on Chemours chemistry.

Chemours is seeking a Project Manager to join our growing Capital Execution team. This position report directly to the Senior Manager – Capital Projects.

As a Project Manager (PM), you will lead large/complex and small capital projects across Chemours sites worldwide that will shape the future of our operations and deliver on our commitment to safety, quality, and innovation. This role offers the unique opportunity to work on diverse, high-impact initiatives while collaborating with teams across the globe. This position may be based at various Chemours locations; however, proximity to our headquarters in the Wilmington, Delaware or Philadelphia, PA area —will enable close collaboration with partner teams.

The Project Manager is responsible for planning, leading, and managing all activities associated with executing capital projects. PM’s are expected to have strong project leadership skills and experience to successfully and safely execute projects. The PM is accountable for the total effort, including design, procurement, construction, project controls, estimating, document management and contractor oversight, typically from FEL thru Start-Up. The PM works closely with key stakeholders during early FEL and commissioning/start-up. The PM leads and manages the project execution processes as described in the Chemours Project System.

The responsibilities of the position include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Is responsible for identifying project team resources and working with appropriate resource managers to secure as well as ensuring that engineering contractor staffing is adequate, to meet project objectives.

  • Ensures all project team members understand and held accountable for their role, responsibilities and expected deliverables.

  • Establish effective communications with the project team to ensure alignment around business objectives, project objectives, and project scopes as well as with the project stakeholders.

  • Leads front-end loading process, including preparation of the project scopes of work, completion of the project estimates, preparation of funding requests and the integrated project schedule, and the development of the production design basis.

  • Proactively drive project scope, cost, schedule and project resources

  • Identify necessary project deliverables and ensure timely completion and sufficient quality

  • Manages changes in the project scope and controls cost within the approved budgets per the project “Management of Change” policy.

  • Drives capital project work processes and practices as described in the Chemours Project System.

  • Leads / facilitates risk identification / mitigation and problem-solving sessions throughout project life to manage schedule, budget, priorities and constraints.

  • Ensures appropriate design standards and agreements with internal and external design resources are followed.

The following is required for this role:

  • A minimum of a bachelor’s degree in any Engineering discipline

  • Minimum 5 years managing capital projects

  • Minimum of 3 years working with a chemical plant environment

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience with field construction or contract management

  • Capable of managing multiple projects simultaneously

  • Ability to execute smaller, less complex projects with limited engagement of supporting resources

  • Strong communication skills

  • Ability to lead by influence

  • Strong team-building skills

  • Experience in working with engineering/design contractors

  • Experience using project scheduling software

  • Smart engineering/design tools knowledge

  • Fluent use of Microsoft Office software

  • Ability to travel approximately 40% of the time

The following is preferred for this role

  • Direct report supervisory experience is a plus

  • Plant operations or maintenance experience is a plus

Competitive Compensation

Comprehensive Benefits Packages

401(k) Match

Employee Stock Purchase Program

Tuition Reimbursement

Company-paid Volunteer Day

Responsibilities

  • Working in partnership with sales teams, strategic and industry partners in assessing the potential application of our products ensuring that optimum systems solutions are provided to new and existing customers.

  • Proven experience of process, tools, and techniques for responding to a customer’s proposals (RFP, RFQ, RFI) and create viable proposals that grow Juniper's business in a driven and opportunity-filled sales environment.

  • Continuously learn and stay ahead of the industry and competitive solutions, products, and services.

  • Enjoy the personal growth career opportunity that comes from exposure to the latest technological innovations and apply these capabilities to address the real-world challenges of our customers.

Education & Experience

  • Minimum of 10 years’ experience in a technical/pre-sales role as a Sales or Systems Engineer.

  • Bachelor's and/or master’s degree in engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, and or related field or equivalent experience.

  • Extensive experience in designing/engineering/consulting on WAN, Data Center, Security, and Cloud technology solutions.

  • Extensive experience in implementing and operating large scale WAN backbone networks.

  • Extensive experience and depth of knowledge around the Juniper product line, key competitors’ products, solutions, and vertical market use cases.

  • Solid interpersonal, relationship, and communication skills with extensive experience in customer-facing sales activities (presenting, whiteboarding etc.) and Exec/C-level engagements.

  • Extensive experience of datacenter network design (EVPN/VXLAN, Clos architectures, underlay fabric)

  • Extensive experience of MPLS and WAN network design (LDP, RSVP, SR-TE, SRv6 etc.)

  • Experience of network security (NGFW, UTM, DDoS, IPSec, MACSec, SIEM)

  • Hands-on experience with either Juniper or other vendors solutions.

What we would love you to have:

  • DevOps experience in automation using Python, Chef, Puppet, Ansible, YANG, JSON, Netconf and Ansible.

  • Experience with cloud-based technologies such as AWS, GCP and Azure

  • JNCIP, JNCIE, CCNP, CCIE, etc. or other industry certification is desired

What makes you a phenomenal fit:

  • Positive attitude, a desire to learn new technologies, and the ability to handle competing priorities in a very challenging environment.

  • Embraces HPE culture and values and acts as an advocate and role model for the brand

  • Must be willing and able to travel as required to meet business and customer demands

title: Solutions Architect - AWS WWPS DoW, US Navy Solutions Architecture
description:
Do you like helping U.S. Department of Defense organizations implement innovative cloud computing solutions and solve technical problems? Would you like to do this using the latest cloud computing technologies? Do you have a knack for helping these groups understand application architectures and integration approaches, and do you have the consultative skills to launch a project on a trajectory to success?

Come join our team as a Solutions Architect (SA) and help us accelerate our growing U.S. Defense Department business as part of the World Wide Public Sector practice. This SA will join a team that supports US Navy, Marine Corps, and other Department of War customers. This is an excellent opportunity to join Amazon’s truly innovative technical teams, while also developing your skills and furthering your career within one of the most innovative and progressive technology companies anywhere.

In this role, you will have the opportunity to help shape and deliver on a strategy to build broad use of Amazon Web Services (e.g., Amazon Bedrock, Amazon SageMaker, Amazon S3, Amazon EC2, and AWS Lambda) directly with customers and our ecosystem of system integrators and solution providers. You will leverage generative AI to solve customer challenges and deliver POCs in their environments. Your broad responsibilities will include: owning the technical engagement and ultimate success around specific implementation projects; defining implementation architectures, developing a deep expertise in the AWS technologies as well as broad know-how around how applications and services are constructed using the AWS platform; and being a subject matter expert on security and other technologies as it relates to customer applications and services.

You will provide thoughtful technical design and offer sensitivity to our customer needs in the Defense markets for cloud computing working with a truly innovative sales and business development team. You will lead efforts to capture and share best-practice knowledge amongst the AWS solution architect community. You will have the opportunity to learn from, collaborate with, and educate some of the brightest technical minds in the industry today across the breadth of enterprise architecture.

You should apply to this role if you are passionate about:
- Creating, building, educating, training and designing cloud computing architectures, especially if it’s for Defense Department customers.
- Getting hands on to experiment, build, and demonstrate technology solutions leveraging the latest AI technologies to expedite delivery and quality.
- Deep-dive technical discussions around design and the curiosity to keep your technical skills current while maintaining a pulse on industry trends
- Our company credo: “Work hard. Have fun. Make history.” It’s critical to love what you do and take pride in your value proposition to our customers.

Experience in the following key areas are helpful:
- Executive Speaking and Presentation Skills – White board, small and large group presentations
- Technical – Experience with AI/GenAI, software development, web applications services development/deployment, DevOps/DevSecOps, cloud computing, data and database architectures and analytics, or networking
- Operational – Web site/services operations, management, and security
- Economic and business – RFP/Acquisition support; technical architecture; understanding market trends; cost benefit analysis
- Advisory/Consulting experience with Defense Department customers

Amazon aims to be the most customer centric company on earth. Amazon Web Services (AWS) provides a highly reliable, scalable, low-cost infrastructure platform in the cloud that powers critical applications for hundreds of thousands of businesses in 190 countries around the world.

This position requires that the candidate selected be a US Citizen and obtain and maintain an active TS security clearance.

title: Field Service Technician I
description:
Clean Harbors in Colton, Ca is seeking a Field Services Technician I to join our safety conscious team. This role will be active in the field responsible for the performance of tasks associated with hazardous waste clean-up, site-remediation, equipment decontamination and handling of hazardous materials.

Clean Harbors is the leading provider of environmental, energy and industrial services throughout the United States, Canada, Mexico and Puerto Rico. Everywhere industry meets environment, Clean Harbors is on-site, providing premier environmental, energy and industrial services. We are solving tough problems through innovation and proven methodology – come be part of the solution with us.

Why work for Clean Harbors?
  • Health and Safety is our #1 priority and we live it 3-6-5!
  • Focus on maintaining sustainability and cleaning the Earth
  • Competitive Pay
  • Comprehensive health benefits coverage after 30 days of full-time employment including 401K with Company match
  • Own part of the company with our Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Opportunities for growth and development for all the stages of your career
  • Company paid training and tuition reimbursement
Key Responsibilities:
  • Ensure Health and Safety is the number one goal by following policies, processes, and always acting in a safe manner
  • Engage in strenuous physical labor including lifting and pulling heavy objects
  • Operate light and heavy equipment, handles various hand tools and powered industrial tools, works with vibration-producing tools
  • Wear and properly use a variety of personal protective Equipment (PPE). Including respirators, skin, face, hand and foot protection in a multiple number of combinations
  • Work in various temperatures indoors and outdoors in all weather conditions
  • Work in atmospheres and locations with the potential for exposure to various chemical and physical agents, some of which may be hazardous, toxic, or corrosive
  • Work in potentially elevated noise levels, confined spaces, including lifting in areas of low clearance
  • Work at elevations including working from ladders and scaffolding
  • Assist in field sampling activities and calibration of meters
  • Climb ladders, scaffolding and into and out of trucks, tanks, and various other containers
  • Work extended (> 8 hrs.) time periods
  • Attend all compliance and safety update meetings
  • Inspect drums for container integrity and regulatory compliance
  • Safe loading and unloading of hazardous and non-hazardous waste
  • Conduct waste stream sampling and profiling as necessary
  • Follow all local, state (provincial) and federal compliance regulations and rules
  • Safely operate vehicles in accordance with U.S. DOT, local, state (provincial) and federal requirements
  • Safely observe all corporate operating guidelines and procedures
  • Observe all company environmental health and safety operating guidelines
  • Perform other duties as assigned
  • By position, ability to be on call for emergency response on rotating basis every other week
  • By position, site-remediation, equipment decontamination, and the handling of hazardous materials

Required Qualifications:

title: Application Developer - ServiceNow
description:
The ServiceNow Developer plays a key part in configuring, customizing, and extending the ServiceNow platform to meet the ever-evolving needs of our business. You will collaborate closely with various departments to understand their challenges and develop innovative solutions that streamline workflows and improve efficiency. This role is very hands on and is a senior expert within the ServiceNow team. Expectations for this role are that the individual delivers new code and application configurations within a formalized Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC). This individual will also foster an environment of mature code development and release and build a strong CI/CD pipeline.

RESPONSIBILITIES, other duties may be assigned

  • Design, develop, and implement custom applications and workflows on the ServiceNow platform

  • Integrate ServiceNow with third-party applications to create a unified IT ecosystem
