    • Provide leadership, coordination, and primary point of contact for internal and external auditors; developing, composing, and implementing corrective action plans, progress reporting, and practice change across the department.

  2. Chief Budget Strategist:

title: Sr. UX Designer, People Engagement Experience (PEX)
description:
The People Engagement Experience (PEX) is the thread across our People Engagement (PE) experiences made up of forward-thinking UX designers, researchers, writers and design technologists. PEX is revolutionizing the user experience for Amazonians across the globe. Our design work has a direct impact on the lives of millions of Amazonians, helping them achieve work-life balance and advance in their careers. We’re also customer-obsessed, driving impact across the company by delivering on user-centered and business needs. We support Amazon's mission to become Earth's best employer through making it easier to acquire, train and retain employees.

As a UX Designer of the PEX team, you will be responsible for the design of the end-to-end employee experience. You’ll craft elegant design solutions across a range of personas and platforms at global scale and collaborate closely with product and engineering partners, as well as multiple partner teams within the broader People Experience Technology (PXT) and Amazon Worldwide Operation orgs. As a Senior Designer you will be a key contributor to transforming the currently fragmented systems into an intuitive, guided journey that supports all aspects of contingent workforce management through a cohesive and efficient product for all stakeholders. You will identify large scope product and long-term design vision to raise the UX bar for this domain.

To succeed in this role, the candidate must be an innovative self-starter in driving operational excellence and a strategic big-picture thinker. The candidate must have proven the ability to succeed in a highly ambiguous, fast-paced environment. Our environment requires the skills to work collaboratively and the commitment to take ownership when needed.

Key job responsibilities
- Assume ownership for the end to end product experiences and features across desktop, mobile and more.
- Manage the user experience design of multiple mid-to-large-sized programs.
- Contribute to the vision for the organization and influence product strategic roadmap. Lead the discovery, strategize concept design and launch phases of a project.
- Champion user-centered design culture. Drive creative process and collaboration with cross-functional partners to propose new ideas and strategies.
- Model behavior that exemplifies Amazon Leadership Principles in their team. Raises the design bar for the organization.
- Provide coaching and feedback, with an emphasis on growing junior Independent Contributors and leadership capability.
- Create and drive adoption of design guidelines, mechanisms, best practices, process and tools.

A day in the life
The Senior UX Designer will be working with product and engineering stakeholders closely on day-to-day basis. While this designer independently owns multiple products/features at the same time, he/she will also collaborate with other UX designers in the same team on connecting individual features to a holistic experience. UX Researcher and UX Content will support you in your work. This designer will share design work regularly with design team peer review, stakeholder review and leadership.

About the team
We are a multidisciplinary team creating truly meaningful products and experiences that empower and connect millions of Amazon employees. Our team consist of designers, researchers and writers, and is very diverse in terms of educational background, race, skills, and location.

title: Public Finance Investment Banking Director – Senior Living
description:
Job Description:

At Piper Sandler, we connect capital with opportunity to build a better future. We enable growth and success of our clients through deep sector expertise, candid advice and a differentiated, highly productive culture. Our mission is to recruit, develop, and retain high-performing people that are bright, committed, and who work in partnership with others to achieve at a high level.

About our Public Finance Group

We are a national public finance investment banking franchise with a diversified business focused on middle market issuers and specialty sector expertise. Our core business is partnering with not-for-profits, private developers, and state and local governments to raise capital for infrastructure projects through the issuance of tax-exempt and taxable bonds. We finance a broad spectrum of projects across our regional footprint and our specialty sector coverage. Learn more about our public finance team here.

We are currently looking for a Public Finance Investment Banking Director to join the public finance Senior Living team. This role can be based in any of our regional offices, offering flexibility for the right candidate regardless of location.

About the Role

The Director will serve as a senior member of the Senior Living team, responsible for leading deal origination, structuring, and execution for clients across the senior living and long-term care sector. We are interested in candidates who bring deep industry expertise, strong relationships, strategic insight, and the ability to develop new business opportunities. This individual will manage day-to-day client relationships, oversee transaction teams, and play a lead role in expanding the firm's presence within the sector. Depending on the candidate’s background, the role may emphasize sector origination, strategic planning, relationship development, and franchise building, with transaction execution responsibilities calibrated to the individual’s experience.

Key Responsibilities

  • Client Relationship Management: Build and sustain strong relationships with senior living providers, not-for-profit sponsors, and other issuers within the sector.
  • Origination & Business Development: Identify and cultivate new client relationships and strategic opportunities; engage senior living leaders in consultative discussions regarding capital needs, growth plans, affiliations, refinancing, campus repositioning, and long-term financial strategy.
  • Transaction Execution: Lead the structuring and execution of bond issuances, refinancings, and other capital markets transactions specific to senior living financings.
  • Quantitative Modeling: Develop and oversee financial models to structure and optimize debt transactions, including calculating debt service and sizing bond issues.
  • Strategic Advisory: Provide expert guidance to clients on capital raising, debt structuring, and long-term financial planning.
  • Team Leadership & Mentorship: Lead and mentor Associates and Analysts, fostering a collaborative, high-performance culture consistent with the group's mentorship-driven approach.
  • Market Intelligence: Maintain a deep understanding of trends, competitive dynamics, and regulatory developments within the senior living and long-term care space.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with internal teams across capital markets, credit, and public finance to deliver comprehensive client solutions.
  • Recruiting & Franchise Building: Contribute to the identification and recruitment of new talent for the group, along with other franchise-building initiatives.

Who We Are Looking For

We are open to candidates from a variety of professional backgrounds, including:

  • Public finance or investment banking;
  • Municipal advisory or financial advisory;
  • Senior living or long-term care operations;
  • Chief financial officer, finance, or development roles at nonprofit senior living organizations;
  • Healthcare finance or real estate finance;
  • Strategic, management, or capital-planning consulting; or
  • Related roles involving senior living strategy, capital formation, debt financing, or institutional relationship development.

The strongest candidates will combine sector credibility, sound financial judgment, strong communication skills, and the ability to build trusted relationships with boards, CEOs, CFOs, developers, lenders, investors, and other sector participants.

Qualifications & Skills

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, or related discipline; MBA a plus.
  • 7+ years of relevant experience in investment banking, public finance, municipal advisory, senior living, long-term care, healthcare finance, consulting, development, or a related field.
  • Familiarity with senior living and long-term care operating models, capital needs, debt structures, and the financing considerations affecting nonprofit and other healthcare providers. Experience with tax-exempt bonds, taxable debt, bank financing, private placements, or municipal finance is preferred but not required for candidates with relevant industry experience.
  • Proven track record of client relationship management and successful transaction execution.
  • Strong financial modeling and analytical capabilities.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Series 52 and 63 and 7 licenses required or willingness to obtain
  • Demonstrated leadership experience, including managing and developing junior team members.

Piper Sandler values a strong culture dedicated to the emotional and physical well-being of our employees. Learn more about our commitment to our employees' health, well-being, our benefits program and how we are here for our employees and their families today, tomorrow and beyond here.

The anticipated starting salary range for individuals expressing interest in this position is $150,000 - $200,000 per year. Placement within this range is dependent upon level of experience, location and other factors. This position is eligible for annual incentive compensation which will be part of the total compensation. Total compensation for this position will be competitive with the market.

title: Mission Capability Leader
description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

The Defense Systems Group (DSG) provides analysis-based decision support to senior leaders on space architectures, policy and strategy, technology development, warfighter capability enablers, systems integration, defense industrial base, and threat reduction to help shape existing and future space missions across the national security space (NSS) enterprise. DSG is unique at Aerospace as it not only directly supports major customers, including the U.S. Space Force, U.S. Space Command, Air Force Material Command, and senior leadership at the Pentagon, but also provides a broad range of technical support across the national space enterprise, maintaining vertical responsibilities with customers’ portfolios as well as horizontal, matrixed responsibilities across the corporation. Additionally, DSG provides deep technical expertise to the Space Force Space Systems Command (SSC) in the conception, design, acquisition, launch and operations of satellite, launch vehicle, ground control, and range systems.

DSG’s Joint and Multi-Domain Subdivision supports a broad sponsor landscape, extending Aerospace’s space-based technical expertise to operational end users. With projects ranging from state-of-the-art research and concept development, to prototyping, cutting-edge laboratory environments, fully integrated operational capabilities, and robust analytics and decision support tools, Aerospace’s support to the military Services, Combatant Commands, and other government agencies helps to enable strategic decisions, explore new operational concepts, and drive toward integrated, multi-domain capabilities.

As the Mission Capability Leader for the HEX mission capability supporting the DAF Integrated Fires Command and Control (DIFC2) program, you will drive the technical vision, architecture, and delivery of advanced capabilities that integrate multi-INT data across the Command, Control, Communications, and Battle Management (C3BM) enterprise. Your work will directly enable Long Range Kill Chain and Sensor to Shooter workflows.

The selected candidate will be required to work full-time, on-site at our facility in Reston, VA.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Define and maintain the end-to-end technical design for the Hex mission capability, including network architecture, interfaces, data flows, and integration points across the C3BM enterprise, Sensor to Shooter workflows, and DAF Battle Network (DBN)
  • Act as the primary technical focal point to the government product owner and stakeholders, bridging operational requirements with architectural and engineering solutions
  • Advise a multi-disciplinary team of multi-INT analysts and developers; set technical expectations and direction, establish standards, review designs, and provide actionable feedback
  • Provide direct technical contributions in areas such as cloud-based capabilities, UI/UX, integration and use of Artificial Intelligence (AI), data integration, and communications systems
  • Coordinate across direct program staff and technical reach-back (Systems Engineering Working Group, Data IPT), and support exercises and surge as needed to meet customer requirements

What You Need to be Successful

Minimum Requirements for the Project Engineer– Software Architecture Engineering:

  • Bachelor’s degree in relevant STEM discipline or closely related technical field
  • Eight or more years of technical experience, including multi-disciplinary systems engineering and technical team leadership
  • Several years of mission capability experience, ideally supporting Sensor to Shooter or comparable operational workflows
  • Experience as a network architect or system-of-systems (SoS) architect, defining end-to-end architectures, interfaces, and data flows across integrated systems
  • Demonstrated ability to engage and align multi-level stakeholders, including government acquisition programs and senior customers (O-6/GS-15 level), to ensure architectural direction reflects both strategic objectives and program constraints.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in small team settings and independently with minimal supervision
  • High level of self-initiative and a demonstrated ability to bring innovative solutions to hard mission problems
  • Willing to travel up to 25 – 50% of the time (~1- 2 weeks per month), including exercises and surge support as required
  • This position requires an active TS/SCI security clearance, issued by the US government. US citizenship is required to obtain a clearance

In addition to the above, the minimum requirements for the Senior Project Engineer - Software Architecture Engineering include:

  • Twelve or more years of technical experience, including multi-disciplinary systems engineering and technical team leadership
  • Extensive experience and expertise in technical areas and leadership mentioned above

How You Can Stand Out

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these:

  • Advanced technical and/or business degree
  • Sensor systems / ISR and sensor-discipline background, with the ability to leverage and communicate this experience to teammates and customers
  • Coding experience in a modern software language such as Python, R, or Java
  • Understanding of Agile development practices, with the ability to act as a product owner for established needs
  • Previous experience supporting the Department of the Air Force and the Portfolio Acquisition Executive (PAE) for C3BM; in-depth knowledge of the C3BM enterprise and Intelligence Community (IC)
  • Applicable SAP/SAR access

Our leadership philosophy is simple: every employee, regardless of level and role, can demonstrate leadership. At Aerospace, our commitment is our people. To cultivate our talent and ensure that we have a strong pipeline of future leaders, we want individuals who:

title: Product Engineer III
description:
Product Engineer III

This position is responsible for the design, development, validation and release of new and/or current production, components, assemblies or mechanisms. It is the Product Engineer’s responsibility to address product development and design issues as required in a timely manner and with a quality focus.


About Linamar/McLaren Engineering

Linamar Corporation is a Canadian diversified global manufacturing company of highly engineered products across global industries and markets. From the entrepreneurial seeds planted by our dynamic founder, to the support provided along the way, all Linamar employees are poised for success in this fast-paced and rapidly growing environment. With access to the tools you need to succeed, you will make an impact along with other motivated and engaged employees. UNIT: The Acute Care Cardiology Unit (ACCU) is an integral part of the Heart Institute and provides comprehensive cardiac care for complex medical and surgical patients. ACCU cares for patients ages newborn to adults, including those with heart failure, pulmonary hypertension, heart and multi-organ transplants, post-procedural care, and congenital heart disease. Therapeutic modalities include noninvasive monitoring, cardiac telemetry, oxygen therapies, feeding tubes, central line access, inotropic/anticoagulation/antiarrhythmic drug therapy, NIRS, and complex drainage tube management. Patients may have additional specialty mechanical pumps, including mechanical circulatory support devices such as the Berlin Heart, the SynCardia total artificial heart, and the HeartMateIII.

  • Compliance - Patient Services Staff - Sustain a working understanding of regulatory requirements and accreditation standards. Support leadership in Compliance efforts to meet and sustain the regulatory compliance efforts of the department and hospital. Be mindful and judicious in monitoring safety and departmental policies and procedures. Ensure all individual certifications and Safety College requirements are fulfilled in a timely basis. Work with department managers, nurse council and magnet representatives to identify and share safety best practices. Be mindful of CCHMCs processes and compliance with CMS standards and freely communicate safety and compliance concerns to leadership team members.

Sustains a working understanding of regulatory requirements and accreditation standards. Ensures individual certifications and Safety College requirements are fulfilled in a timely basis. Is mindful of CCHMCs processes and compliance with CMS standards and freely communicates safety and compliance concerns to leadership team members.

  • Clinical judgment when performing caring practices - Collects clinical data; follow algorithms, decision trees, and protocols. Matches formal knowledge with clinical events to make appropriate decisions; uses available resources as needed. Documents plan of care, care delivered, and patient and family outcomes. Focuses on the usual and customary needs of the patient and family; anticipates future needs; bases care on standards and protocols; maintains a safe physical environment; acknowledges death as a potential outcome. Consistently integrates age specific concepts into patient care, taking into consideration both the patient's chronological age and developmental functioning. Using self-management support, develops care goals and actions through partnerships with patients and families. Demonstrates openness to coaching and mentoring from others. Facilitates learning by assisting with peer and student learning experiences. Works with department managers, nurse council and magnet representatives to identify, share, implement and evaluate safety best practices.

  • Exhibits advocacy, moral agency and response to inclusion - Works on behalf of patient and family; assesses personal values; aware of ethical conflicts/issues that may surface in clinical setting; makes ethical/moral decisions based on rules; represents patient when patient cannot represent self; aware of patients' rights. Assesses cultural inclusion. Recognizes the potential impact of culture on the patient/family experience, and incorporates culturally inclusive concepts into patient care.

  • Patient Care - Age Specific and Culturally Inclusive - Consistently integrates age specific and culturally inclusive concepts into patient care, taking into consideration both the patient's chronological age and developmental functioning.

title: Principal Battery Engineer
description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.

Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.

Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.

Role Description

Form Energy is hiring a Principal Battery Engineer to join the Product Echem Performance team. In this role, you will be a technical leader in developing the next round of optimization in our Iron-Air technology through improved sensor strategy and cell state identification. As a member of the Core Tech organization, you will be at the forefront of development and product implementation of the Iron-Air technology. Your responsibilities will also include leading RCAs for unexplained electrochemical phenomena observed in the field from our first deployments and implementing correction actions long term into the product development plans for future generation of products. This role is crucial in ensuring the successful scale up via technology optimization and customer experience throughout product operation and lifetime. This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission!

Relocation assistance is available.

What you'll do:

  • Develop electrochemical signal strategy for the basis of state algorithms including hands-on work testing novel sensors or measurement methods. Create a roadmap for cell internal state determination.

  • Own cost analysis of electrochemical sensor inclusion and performance optimization resulting from improved cell internal state determination.

  • Establish state of the art prototype testing capabilities for electrochemical sensor evaluation in the Berkeley, CA facility.

  • Lead RCAs on product-level electrochemical phenomena impacting performance; establish framework/approach in this space during initial deployments.

What you'll bring:

  • PhD or MS with 10+ years of professional experience in Battery or Electrochemical Engineering.

  • Hands on lab expertise and agility to navigate prototyping environment to balance safety, timelines, and quality of novel testing.

  • Experience in leading technical teams through RCAs and excellent data analysis skills.

  • Experience with battery/cell state estimation, signal processing, or sensor integration into a production system.

#LI-Onsite

Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.

When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.

To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.


If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.

As TI expands its manufacturing footprint, the LFAB2 fab project is a critical part of our long-term growth roadmap and competitive advantage. We are in the early phases of building construction and MERFEI installation, creating unique opportunities to help shape a major factory project from the ground up. We are looking for motivated, capable individuals who want to work on a fast-paced, high-impact project and help deliver a world-class manufacturing environment. The LFAB Commissioning Lead will:

  • Own and manage the facilities expansion site-wide commissioning program, including development and maintenance of the master commissioning plan, system turnover packages, and commissioning schedules
  • Lead QA/QC oversight across all trade contractors, ensuring inspection and test plans (ITPs) are in place, executed, and documented for all scopes of work
  • Drive pre-functional and functional testing activities for all MERFEI systems, building systems, and process support utilities including cleanroom HVAC, ultra-pure water (UPW), chemical distribution, electrical power, and building automation systems (BMS)
  • Coordinate system walkdowns, punch list generation, and punch list resolution in partnership with the Construction Manager, trade contractors, and TI's D&E discipline leads
  • Partner with TI Fab Operations to align commissioning sequencing with tool qualification milestones and operational readiness requirements
  • Establish and enforce project-wide quality standards, non-conformance reporting (NCR) procedures, and corrective action processes
  • Review and approve contractor quality submittals including ITPs, method statements, and commissioning procedures
  • Track and report commissioning progress, open punch items, and system turnover status to TI's Project Manager and key stakeholders
  • Identify risks to commissioning schedule and quality outcomes; drive corrective and preventive actions to resolution
  • Maintain complete and auditable commissioning and quality records for all systems; compile and deliver final turnover documentation packages to TI at project closeout
  • Coordinate with the BIM Information Coordinator and Design Coordinator to ensure as-built conditions and field resolutions are accurately reflected in project documentation prior to system turnover
  • Participate in construction progress meetings, and commissioning readiness reviews as the quality and commissioning lead
  • Standardize processes across the site and roll out and align with global QAQC/CX processes across TI

Texas Instruments will not sponsor job applicants for visas or work authorization for this position.

Minimum Requirements:

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Construction Management, or related degree/field
  • 5 years of relevant experience supporting facilities and/or project teams

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated strong customer service orientation and ability to take ownership for issue resolution
  • Knowledge of fab non-process and process systems including cleanroom HVAC, ultra-pure water, chemical distribution, electrical power systems, and building automation
  • Experience supporting semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, or large-scale industrial construction projects in a commissioning or QA/QC leadership capacity
  • Familiarity with MERFEI systems installation, pre-functional testing, and functional performance testing
  • Experience developing and executing commissioning plans, inspection and test plans (ITPs), and system turnover packages
  • Experience managing punch list processes across multiple trade contractors and coordinating multi-discipline system closeout
  • Familiarity with non-conformance reporting (NCR) processes and corrective action management
  • Experience coordinating with Fab Operations or end-user teams on operational readiness and tool qualification sequencing
  • Experience with construction planning, scheduling, and progress-tracking tools or related technologies such as BIM, generative scheduling, and automated progress tracking
  • Strong communication, collaboration, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, work effectively in a fast-paced team environment, and drive results with urgency and ownership
  • Demonstrated strong analytical and problem solving skills
  • Ability to work in teams and collaborate effectively with people in different functions
  • Ability to take the initiative and drive for results
  • Strong time management skills that enable on-time project delivery
  • Ability to work effectively in an interrupt-driven, fast-paced and rapidly changing environment

  • Demonstrated ability to build strong, influential relationships

description:
Ben jij een gestructureerde student die energie krijgt van het organiseren van informatie, samenwerken met internationale teams en het verbeteren van digitale processen? Dan zijn wij op zoek naar jou.

Je helpt bij vertaalprocessen, bewaakt contentkwaliteit en zorgt ervoor dat collega's wereldwijd eenvoudig toegang hebben tot de juiste informatie.

Je werkt nauw samen met verschillende afdelingen en internationale stakeholders en speelt een centrale rol in het stroomlijnen van een complex vertaal- en contentproces.

  • Afstemmen met (internationale) afdelingen over vertalingen, prioriteiten en deadlines.
  • Bewaken van workflows en zorgen voor een gestructureerde en tijdige oplevering.
  • Controleren van de kwaliteit en consistentie van vertaalde content.
  • Samenwerken met sales & services, clusters en business teams om content succesvol te implementeren.

Je bent een nauwkeurige en zelfstandige doener die zich prettig voelt in een dynamische, internationale omgeving. Je werkt gestructureerd, communiceert helder en weet overzicht te houden in processen met meerdere stakeholders en deadlines.

Daarnaast herken jij jezelf in het volgende:

  • MBO+ of HBO werk- en denkniveau.
  • Uitstekende beheersing van het Engels, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk.

  • Ervaring met online tools of contentmanagementsystemen, ervaring met Showpad is een pré.

Je kunt meedoen aan Hyrox-workouts of je inschrijven voor personal training – en je collega’s uitdagen tijdens een actieve pauze.

title: DevOps Engineer

DevOps Engineer

Overview

Job Summary:

The DevOps Engineer is a technical operational engineering role responsible for improving DevOps, Release Management, Test Automation, and platform operations through intelligent automation, operational tooling, observability, and AI-enabled capabilities. This role focuses on building scalable operational solutions that improve system reliability, reduce manual operational effort, strengthen production visibility, and optimize engineering support workflows across the Connected and OBE programs.

The DevOps Engineer partners closely with Engineering, DevOps, Production Support, Architecture, and Release teams to identify improvement opportunities, streamline operational processes, and implement practical solutions across monitoring, incident management, deployment operations, operational analytics, release coordination, and support workflows. This role is expected to independently drive operational change, collaborate with peer teams and senior DevOps engineers, and influence adoption of scalable automation and AI-assisted engineering practices. This role contributes to implementing operational tooling, automation frameworks, intelligent monitoring capabilities, and AI-assisted solutions that improve operational efficiency, engineering effectiveness, and platform stability.

This is a hands-on engineering role focused on applying modern operational engineering practices to solve enterprise operational challenges through automation, operational intelligence, and scalable engineering solutions. The DevOps Engineer helps improve operational scalability, support responsiveness, operational maturity, and engineering efficiency while aligning enterprise technology and governance standards.

Responsibilities

Essential Functions:

  • Design, develop, and maintain intelligent operational solutions, automation workflows, scripts, integrations, and orchestration capabilities across DevOps, Release Management, Test Automation, and operational ecosystems.
  • Identify operational bottlenecks, repetitive support activities, and manual engineering processes suitable for automation and operational optimization.
  • Independently drive operational improvement initiatives from discovery through implementation, partnering with peer teams, senior DevOps engineers, and cross-functional stakeholders to deliver measurable process and automation outcomes.
  • Implement AI-enabled operational capabilities focused on incident visibility, monitoring, alert correlation, workflow automation, operational analytics, engineering efficiency, and AI-assisted development practices using tools such as GitHub Copilot, Claude, or similar platforms.

title: Senior Systems Engineer
description:
About Amentum

Amentum is a global leader in advanced engineering and innovative technology solutions, trusted by the United States and its allies to address their most significant and complex challenges in science, security and sustainability. Our people apply undaunted curiosity, relentless ambition and boundless imagination to challenge convention and drive progress. Our commitments are underpinned by the belief that safety, collaboration and well-being are integral to success. Headquarters in Chantilly, Virginia, we have approximately 50,000 employees in more than 70 countries across all 7 continents.

About the Role

Amentum is seeking a motivated and results-driven Senior Systems Engineer to support the Naval Surface Warfare Center (NSWC) Dahlgren Division, H20. In this dynamic role, you will provide technical oversight and expertise for the development of the AN/SQQ-89 Advanced Baselines, primarily focusing on surface Anti-Submarine Warfare (ASW) functional areas, including Contact Management and Weapons Control.

Responsibilities:

- Technical Oversight: Provide guidance to integrator developers, ensuring performance and interface requirements are met for the AN/SQQ-89 Advanced Baselines.

- Engineering Analysis: Conduct comprehensive engineering reviews, including but not limited to:

- Performance Specification (P-Spec) baseline releases

- Functional Description Document (FDD) baseline releases

- Interface Design Specifications (IDS)

Requirements Management: Actively participate in the AN/SQQ-89 Requirements Working Group to address performance requirements for Cruiser-Destroyer (CRUDES) platforms and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) baselines.

  • Subject Matter Expertise: Participate in Bug Adjudication Board meetings to analyze reported issues within installed baselines.

Required Qualifications:

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, scientific, or technical discipline from an accredited institution, or

  • Ten (10) years of relevant, demonstrated experience in combat systems, command & control systems, and simulation/stimulation systems related to Surface Ship Undersea Warfare (USW) for U.S. and Foreign Military Sales (FMS) platforms.

Experience: minimum of ten (10) years of professional systems engineering experience in support of Undersea Warfare, including the following:

  • At least five (5) years as a team leader performing systems analysis, engineering, and mission planning efforts.

  • Proficiency in identifying, analyzing, and resolving complex engineering challenges within platform, weapon, C2, and combat systems for Navy/Joint Warfighting capabilities.

  • Experience with both Government Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) and Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) software technologies.

  • Demonstrated ability to develop system integration documentation for weapons and C2 systems, including Engineering Change Proposals (ECPs), Interface Change Requests (ICRs), Interface Design Specifications (IDS), and Weapon Specifications (WS).

  • Familiarity with weapons and combat system certification processes, including self-certification criteria.

  • Previous experience with Foreign Military Sales (FMS) programs.

  • Willingness to work onsite at NSWC Dahlgren.

Desired Qualifications:

  • Experience in top-level system architecture design and program requirement development.

  • Knowledge of maintaining, reviewing, generating, and tracking systems engineering documentation.

  • Expertise in evaluating and refining existing system requirements and supporting upgrades.

  • Ability to review and contribute to Concept of Operations (CONOPS) and Concept of Employment (CONEMP) documents.

  • Experience supporting technology refresh initiatives, providing insight on COTS technologies.

The Groundman position is your first step to a rewarding career in the construction and maintenance of our nation's Power Grid. You will assist your team in building, repairing, and maintaining overhead electrical distribution systems. You will report to the Foreman.

title: Product Manager — Finance ERP, Accounting Transformation Group
description:
Amazon is seeking an experienced Product Manager to own the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for the Finance ERP capabilities that power Amazon's global Accounting and Finance operations. This leader will work backwards from Accounting, Controllership, and Finance customers to determine what to build, prioritize investments, and deliver measurable business outcomes.
The ideal candidate combines strong product judgment with deep Finance ERP domain expertise across General Ledger, Consolidation, Record-to-Report, subledgers, intercompany, and leading ERP platforms such as SAP S/4HANA or Oracle ERP. This role partners closely with Accounting, Finance, FinTech, Engineering, and Internal Controls to translate complex accounting needs into scalable ERP solutions.


Key job responsibilities
•Own the end-to-end Finance ERP product vision, strategy, and roadmap across Accounting domains and adjacent solution stacks.
•Work backwards from Accounting, Controllership, and Finance customers to identify needs, develop use cases, and prioritize capabilities across General Ledger, Consolidation, and related processes.
• Define business and product requirements and partner with technology teams to design, build, integrate, and deliver scalable ERP capabilities.
• Lead Proof of Concepts and solution assessments to validate that proposed ERP capabilities meet business, controllership, scalability, and performance requirements.
• Represent the customer throughout the delivery lifecycle, including integration testing, UAT, deployment, and hypercare; validate solutions against Accounting requirements and drive readiness decisions.
• Apply deep Finance and Accounting process knowledge across areas such as General Ledger, receivables, payables, assets, project accounting, cost accounting, consolidation.
• Own controllership, compliance, and auditability outcomes and ensure these requirements are incorporated into ERP product priorities and solution design.
• Drive product strategy and phasing for large-scale ERP modernization, process standardization, General Ledger transformation, and migration from legacy platforms.
• Drive alignment across Accounting, Finance, Engineering, and other stakeholders, navigating ambiguity and making clear prioritization and tradeoff decisions.
• Communicate product direction, business cases, metrics, risks, and tradeoffs effectively to stakeholders and senior leadership.

A Product Manager on this team leads large-scale Accounting transformation by setting the direction for Amazon's Finance ERP capabilities. They work directly with Accounting and Controllership customers to identify problems, shape future-state solutions, prioritize the roadmap, validate capabilities through POCs and testing, and partner with Engineering to deliver solutions that improve scalability, controllership, and operational efficiency.

About the team
Accounting Transformation Group drives initiatives that modernize accounting processes, improve controllership, and enable scalable growth across Amazon. The team operates at the intersection of Accounting, Finance, process design, and technology to build scalable financial capabilities and support new business models.

title: Software Engineer III- Eng
description:
Why UKG:

At UKG, the work you do matters. The code you ship, the decisions you make, and the care you show a customer all add up to real impact. Today, tens of millions of workers start and end their days with our workforce operating platform. Helping people get paid, grow in their careers, and shape the future of their industries. That’s what we do.

We never stop learning. We never stop challenging the norm. We push for better, and we celebrate the wins along the way. Here, you’ll get flexibility that’s real, benefits you can count on, and a team that succeeds together. Because at UKG, your work matters—and so do you.

About the Team:

We are seeking a highly motivated Software Engineer III to join our Engineering Platform Continuous Delivery HCM team. The ideal candidate is passionate about automating software release processes, building reliable deployment pipelines, and improving engineering productivity through modern CI/CD practices. You will play a key role in designing, implementing, and operating the release automation platform that orchestrates UKG Pro product deployments across hybrid cloud and datacenter environments — keeping developer experience smooth and production deployments dependable.

About the Role:

  • Software Development & Automation
    • Develop JavaScript/Node.js automation tools that orchestrate multi-step deployment processes.
    • Build PowerShell and Bash scripts for Windows service management, IIS operations, and environment configuration.
    • Continuously eliminate manual toil by automating repetitive operational tasks (e.g., SU YAML updates, nightly custom deployments, bulk server updates)
    • Explore and implement AI-powered tooling to enhance developer productivity and deployment insight.

    • Platform Engineering
      • Manage and evolve the server inventory system backed by GCP Firestore and internal inventory APIs.
      • Build and maintain self-hosted GitHub Actions runner infrastructure, including pre-scaling and cleanup workflows.
      • Design Deployment Protection Rule (DPR) workflows and approval gates to enforce change control at the pipeline level.
      • Develop reusable workflow components and internal tooling that reduce toil for the broader engineering organization.

    • Platform Operations
      • Monitor pipeline health, deployment status, and server-level outcomes using observability tooling.
      • Troubleshoot production deployment failures, perform root cause analysis, and implement preventive measures.
      • Maintain service stop/start scripts, IIS management automation, and post-deployment validation workflows.
      • Respond to and resolve operational issues across GCP and on-premises server fleets.

    • Infrastructure & Reliability
      • Manage hybrid server infrastructure spanning datacenter regions and GCP.
      • Implement and maintain SSH-based Windows server management via Ansible.
      • Ensure deployment reliability through Firestore state tracking and multi-phase validation workflows.
      • Support rollback capabilities and disaster recovery for production deployments.

    • Technical Leadership
      • Participate in architecture discussions and technical design reviews for the CD platform.
      • Review automation code to ensure quality, maintainability, security, and adherence to best practices.
      • Mentor team members on CI/CD patterns, GCP services, and release engineering practices.

    • DevOps Ownership
      • Take end-to-end ownership of platform services from design and implementation through deployment, monitoring, and production support.
      • Partner closely with development, SRE, Cloud Platform, security, operations, product, and platform stakeholders to align priorities and resolve dependencies.
      • Own security vulnerability remediation across team repositories, including CVE triage, dependency upgrades, and Engineering Portal security updates.

    • Documentation
      • Create and maintain documentation for deployment processes, pipeline architecture, operational runbooks, and automation workflows.

    Basic Qualifications:

title: PKI Operations Engineer
description:
PKI Operations Engineer

Ft. Meade, MD — Full Time (Hybrid)

August Schell is looking for a PKI Operations Engineer to sustain and operate DoD enterprise Public Key Infrastructure in support of our DISA customer. This is a Red Hat Certificate System (RHCS) solution. Where our PKI Software Engineer builds the next-generation certificate-systems code, this role keeps the infrastructure running: operating and hardening the live RHCS environment, standing up new customers and enclaves, driving CVE remediation and patch cycles, monitoring system health, and automating the operational toil that keeps a high-volume CA reliable. The engineer works hand-in-hand with commercial product engineering, government operations teams, and other program contractors — including through the environment's post-quantum cryptography (PQC) migration.

Individuals in this role must be able to work hybrid and go on site at Fort Meade as requested.

Responsibilities Include

  • Operate and sustain the production PKI environment on Red Hat Certificate System (RHCS) — CA availability, certificate lifecycle operations, and the day-to-day health of the issuance pipeline

  • Run RA/CRL/OCSP operations and certificate lifecycle management, including the transition to shorter-lived certificates at higher issuance volume (ACME automation)

  • Onboard new customers, enclaves, and use cases onto the PKI — configuration, integration, and secure hardening of new environments to program standards

  • Own CVE remediation and patch management for the PKI stack and its underlying RHEL hosts — track, test, schedule, and apply security patches with minimal disruption to CA operations

  • Monitor system health and performance; build and maintain alerting, logging, and dashboards; respond to and resolve operational incidents, and lead root-cause analysis

  • Operate and troubleshoot HSM integrations (Entrust nShield / Thales Luna) supporting CA operations and key escrow

  • Automate operational tasks — health checks, backups, certificate/CRL monitoring, deployment and configuration — using scripting and CI/CD tooling to reduce toil and manual error

  • Support the program's PQC migration from an operations standpoint (algorithm rollout, version transition, validation in the live environment)

  • Provide development support in an operational capacity as additional value — small fixes, config-as-code, tooling, and reproduction of issues for the product engineering team — without owning the core feature-development backlog

  • Communicate clearly across government operations stakeholders, commercial vendor engineering, and program contractors; document runbooks and escalate risks and blockers before they impact operations

Requirements

  • Active Secret clearance minimum (Top Secret preferred and may be required)

  • Local to the DMV area with the ability to work on site at Fort Meade as requested

  • Five (5)+ years of relevant systems/operations engineering experience (flexible for candidates with exceptional PKI depth)

  • Strong Linux (RHEL) systems administration and operations background, including patch management and system hardening

  • Knowledge or experience with Linux containers and container orchestration (Podman / Docker) and VMs (KVM)

  • Hands-on experience operating PKI, x.509, cryptography, and system/software security technologies

  • Direct experience operating Red Hat Certificate System (RHCS) — this is a Red Hat solution. Dogtag PKI experience (RHCS's upstream open-source project) is an accepted alternative skillset, as is comparable enterprise CA platform operations (EJBCA, Microsoft AD CS, Entrust Authority, ISC CertAgent, or similar)

  • Scripting/automation proficiency (Python, Bash, or similar) for operational tooling

  • DoD 8570/8140 IAT Level II certification (Security+ or equivalent)

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a habit of documenting runbooks and operational procedures

Stand Out With

  • Prior DISA or DoD PKI program operations experience (Purebred, derived credentials, RA/CRL/OCSP operations at scale)

  • HSM operations experience (Entrust nShield, Thales Luna) — the customer runs Entrust HSMs

  • ACME protocol and certificate automation at scale

  • Post-quantum cryptography familiarity (ML-DSA/Dilithium, Kyber, CNSA 2.0 timelines) from a migration/operations lens

  • Configuration management and infrastructure-as-code (Ansible, or similar)

  • Directory Server / LDAP operations experience

  • Monitoring/observability tooling (Prometheus/Grafana, ELK, or similar) and incident response

  • Agile / ITSM operating rhythms (Scrum, JIRA, change management)

location: United States of America - Texas - Houston
description:

Job Description:

Please note, only one early career application per candidate.

About bp

As a leading global energy company with a presence in 61 countries, bp’s purpose is to deliver energy to the world, today and tomorrow. We are one of only a few companies that can deliver energy – at scale – to countries and millions of customers every day. With more than 100 years of experience, we bring together technology, innovation and deep expertise that keeps communities moving – and we’re still evolving.

About Capital Development and wells

The Capital Development technical function is part of bp’s upstream business and includes both subsurface and wells.

Our wells strategy has four focus areas: Safety First, People, Business Ownership and Responsible Operator. They should be at the center of everything we do. Together, they drive performance, support growth, build a safe, sustainable future and strengthen the value we create for bp.

About the role

As a first step, nothing prepares you better for a career with us than an internship. Our internship program provides hands-on, career-specific experience working full-time during the summer. You will work on real projects that deliver tangible benefits and measurable results. At the same time, you will have the opportunity to learn about and help to solve some of the most important issues we face. You will experience genuine teamwork, and work alongside highly qualified and experienced colleagues, while you work on live projects and operations, using the latest equipment and technology.

Taking on the role as a Wells Engineering intern means working with a multidisciplinary team alongside experienced career professionals across wells, subsurface and HSE, among others. You will be introduced to wells engineering and gain exposure to how we design, construct, troubleshoot and optimize wells.

Wells Engineering encompasses the design, construction and maintenance of wells to safely and reliably extract hydrocarbons. It spans three key disciplines: Drilling Engineering, Completion Engineering and Intervention / Subsea Engineering.

What does a Drilling Engineer do?

Drilling engineers conceptualize, design, plan and oversee well construction, ensuring wells are drilled efficiently, cost-effectively and, above all, safely for people and the environment.

  • You design the well: How many hole sections? What path should it take? What materials will withstand the temperatures and pressures? What drilling fluids and cement will provide barriers?
  • You troubleshoot in real time during well construction: If the drill hits unexpected obstacles (like a high-pressure sand or tool failures), you support the offshore team by adjusting the plan and mobilizing contingencies.
  • You leverage technology to drive efficiency and reliability: From intelligent drilling tools to reducing emissions, you’ll help innovate the future of energy.

What does a Completion Engineer do?

Completion engineers design the system that converts a drilled wellbore into a safe and efficient production or injection system. They “tune up” the wells to maximize production safely and efficiently.

As a completion engineer, you will:

  • Design how wells are prepared for production: selecting the right equipment and techniques to optimize flow.
  • Implement smart solutions: from advance hydraulic fracturing to smart well completions to enhance and control the productivity of reservoirs.
  • Solve complex challenges: like preventing sand from entering the well or managing extreme pressures.
  • Work at the cutting edge: implementing new technologies for enhanced recovery and environmental protection.

What does an Intervention / Subsea engineer do?

Well intervention engineers diagnose issues and perform repairs to get wells back to peak performance when production drops or problems arise.

As a well intervention/subsea engineer you will:

  • Troubleshoot underperforming wells: analyzing data to identify why production has declined.
  • Design corrective treatments: from injection of chemicals such as acid to dissolve scale to mechanical repairs such as changing valves and other components.
  • Oversee complex operations: like running specialist diagnostic tools into the well or changing failed components.
  • Managing the integrity of the wells: monitoring critical well conditions, preventing and remediating failures.
  • Maximize well life: extending production while maintaining safety and efficiency.
  • Manage subsea well interfaces: including subsea wellheads, subsea Christmas trees systems, and subsea interventions systems to enable completion and intervention operations in deepwater fields.

Wells engineering interns may get the opportunity to go offshore as part of their development. This will require completing specific training to travel offshore and meet offshore safety and emergency response requirements (such as HUET). Candidates will also need to get a valid TWIC card (Transportation Workers Identification Credential). The team will provide new hires with further guidance during onboarding.

Successful interns may be considered for a full-time role within our One wells development programme upon earning their degree. One Wells is our early careers programme designed to create a pipeline of wells professionals. Early careers will follow a structured development offer to accelerate the acquisition of foundational technical skills, experience and knowledge, and application in the business world. The programme supports transition from university to discipline professional and provides a framework of ‘non-technical’ skills to support building personal effectiveness skills. Early careers will build their experience through challenging development assignments, grow a toolkit of transferable skills for the future, and have a dedicated network of support to help them succeed.

Our internships

Make an impact on cutting-edge projects. Help find solutions to complex challenges. Be part of a company that invests in you and your growth. You can do it all as an intern at bp. Our 12-week summer programme gives you the opportunity to build your technical knowledge, develop key skills and learn more about life at bp. You'll be part of one team throughout your internship, supported by a dedicated line manager and buddy. There will be opportunities to connect with other interns, take part in training, and grow your network across the business.

Some of the wonderful things you’ll experience as a bp intern are:

  • Project based roles for 12 weeks
  • Typically for students between their penultimate and final year in program
  • Assigned a buddy/mentor to help you transition into bp
  • Attend events consist of networking, lunch & learn, executive calls, webinars, and community service opportunities across locations
  • Comprehensive performance assessment process (goal setting, setting deliverables for projects, mid-term review, and final presentation)
  • Retirement savings opportunities
  • bp provided corporate housing with furnished apartments
  • Relocation assistance (if eligible)

Minimum Requirements for the wells engineer internship

  • Working toward a Bachelor’s degree in Petroleum Engineering, Reservoir Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Chemical Engineering or closely related discipline.
  • Graduating between December 2027 and May 2028
  • Current Cumulative GPA Minimum 3.2
  • Eligible to work in the U.S. with no restrictions (bp will not support U.S. Immigration sponsorship for full-time or long-term employment)

  • At least 2 years of experience with cloud-based ML platforms (AWS, Google Cloud, and/or Azure) and MLOps technologies such as Docker and MLflow in enterprise or production environments.

  • At least 3 years of experience working in Agile software development environments, including code reviews, version control, automated testing, CI/CD practices, and delivering solutions in situations with evolving requirements and ambiguity

It would be great if you had. . . .

  • Strong problem-solving skills and a passion for staying current with advancements in machine learning, NLP, generative AI, and related technologies.

  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to influence decision-making across technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively with peers, present technical work, incorporate feedback, and drive continuous improvement.

What will you be doing in this role?

  • Identify strategic information needs of internal or external clients and translate these into effective, performant and impactful AI solutions.

  • Work in collaboration with other Data Scientists to create solutions that support professional, highly skilled decision makers in their innovation workflow.

  • Explore existing data for insights and recommend additional sources of data for improvements.

  • Perform exploratory analysis to uncover insights and identify opportunities for innovation.

  • Design and execute experiments to validate hypotheses and measure business impact.

  • Collaborate with engineering teams to ensure successful integration and deployment of solutions into production environments.

  • Communicate findings, recommendations, and technical concepts clearly to diverse audiences.

  • Contribute to the adoption of best practices in machine learning, experimentation, and model evaluation.

Product you will be developing

We are mainly using Python for model and code development, you can use whatever IDE & tools you like best (we have people using PyCharm, Databricks, Jupyter Notebook, …), model deployment is on either AWS or Google Cloud depending on the internal customer’s preference, projects are assigned on a quarterly basis but most span multiple quarters up to a year and a half. Over the past 2 decades, we’ve covered everything from UX experiments, decision support systems, search engines, information extraction, machine learning, generative AI – you name it. So the work you’ll be doing will be quite varied and allow you to expand and apply your knowledge on all the latest developments in the AI/ML/MLP domains.

About the team

Within a larger Data Science, Search and Content team of about 100 people (of which 40+ are Data Scientists and ML Engineers), we are a team of 8 Data Scientists located in Belgium, Spain & the US that work predominantly on IP data and products (trademarks, patents and case law for both) though we do the occasional sidestep to other domains as well. We interact with Clarivate’s Product, Sales, Marketing and Operations divisions on a regular basis to make sure we deliver optimal internal and external customer value. With multiple Principal Data Scientists in the team, we can offer excellent support to help you grow in your role. Also, while a lot of work we do originates from customer requests, we also do a fair share of explorative and POC work to help our internal customers understand the business value of the latest technologies.

Hours of Work

This is a permanent full-time contract, we work regular CET hours in Europe, in a hybrid model, with flexibility to accommodate a healthy work-life balance.

We comply with applicable laws and regulations governing non-discrimination in all locations.

title: Senior Product Manager, Acquisition & Brand
description:
About Tin Can

Tin Can is building a safer, simpler way for kids to connect — without smartphones. We're creating screen-free, delightful devices and services that let families call the people who matter most, free from the noise of today's digital world.

We're building a bold, authentic, nostalgic, and kinda quirky brand that resonates with folks who want something simpler & better for their kids than the tech-infused lives we're currently living (and who have a sense of humor about it).

The Role

We're seeking a super-creative (and whacky) Product Manager to drive new customer acquisition and bring brand initiatives to life.

This role requires both analytical and creative horsepower. The "product" you own lives on and off the screen. One day you might map out all the technical systems that need to integrate with a new referral sharing software, and the next you'll help figure out the most rad friendship-bracelet referral reward program and how to get it in kids' hands (err, wrist). You have great taste, you’re not afraid to be bold, and you know how to bring things onto the screen and into real life, no matter what it takes. You’re not just a dreamer, you’re a doer.

Working closely with our Creative, Brand, and Growth Marketing teams is a core (and extremely fun) part of this role. The perfect candidate loves to help turn pie-in-the-sky ideas into reality, while balancing the myriad of possibilities against realities of the business. You say yes more than no, but still, you know when to say no.

What You'll Do

  • Own our referral program, making it a core component of our growth engine

  • Build a kid-to-kid sharing program so Tin Can gets hyped everywhere they go, and the best way to reach them is in the real (non-digital) world

  • Give Growth Marketing the tools and systems to move fast, from landing pages to attribution

  • Support bringing brand campaigns and experiences to life, on and off the screen, from concept through execution

  • Be a partner to Brand, shaping ambitious ideas with them, not just executing on their behalf

  • Align Creative, Growth Marketing, and Engineering on what's next, stitching dreams into reality

  • Get scrappy when the job calls for it — whatever it takes to make something real

What We're Looking For

  • 5+ years of product management experience, ideally with experience in growth or brand; bonus points for work with a brand that gets it

  • You get ish done, rallying diverse groups, finding resources, keeping everyone on track

  • Crystal clear communication, from prank call campaigns to attribution pipelines

  • Experience collaborating closely with designers, creatives, and supply chain teams

  • Excellent visual taste; you know something's great the moment you see it (we call it razzle-dazzle) (jk, nobody actually calls it that)

  • Technical and data fluency — you get numbers, think in systems, understand scaling

  • Fluency using AI as a multiplier in your work; this is how we work, not a nice-to-have

  • Ownership mindset — you're a PM, but also a "call everywhere in Seattle to estimate sticker cost"-er when it counts

  • Low ego, high enthusiasm — you cheer as loud for someone else's idea as your own

Why Join Tin Can

  • We're building tech that protects childhood: We're on a quest to give kids a more analog childhood — one with real conversations, real connection, and way less screen time. No doomscrolling, data mining, or dopamine traps — just a simpler, better way for kids to stay in touch. This is a rare opportunity to build something that truly matters.

  • You'll turn pie-in-the-sky into real life: Acquisition and brand are where some of our wildest ideas get made real, and you'll be the one making it happen, with real ownership over how you get there.

  • Small, high-trust team: Every company says "team," but at Tin Can it means something different. We're a small, mission-driven group that genuinely has each other's backs — professionally and personally. You'll be joining a tight-knit crew where your ideas and instincts matter from day one.

  • Room to explore, not just execute: You'll have the space to explore new ideas, challenge assumptions, and shape a product experience that reflects our values of trust, simplicity, and care.

If you're excited by the idea of turning a wild idea into something kids actually beg for, please reach out. We can't wait to meet someone who's ready to jump in, make things happen, and help us grow.

description:
At Children’s Wisconsin, we believe kids deserve the best.

Children’s Wisconsin is a nationally recognized health system dedicated solely to the health and well-being of children. We provide primary care, specialty care, urgent care, emergency care, community health services, foster and adoption services, child and family counseling, child advocacy services and family resource centers. Our reputation draws patients and families from around the country.

We offer a wide variety of rewarding career opportunities and are seeking individuals dedicated to helping us achieve our vision of the healthiest kids in the country. If you want to work for an organization that makes a difference for children and families, and encourages you to be at your best every day, please apply today.

Please follow this link for a closer look at what it’s like to work at Children’s Wisconsin:

Job Summary:
Augments the Public Safety leadership team and provides shift leadership in the absence of or in collaboration with the Supervisor and Lead Officers. Engaged in the department training program and serves as a trainer for Public Safety staff. Patrols assigned areas of facilities and grounds and responds to emergent and routine situations and calls for service. Performs inspection tours and investigates incidents, as well as general office or record keeping tasks. Verbally de-escalates and if needed, physically restrains patients or disruptive individuals. Performs Weapon Screening services to prevent weapons and other prohibited property from entering CW owned/leased properties. Liaison with MRMC Campus Public Safety/Security departments, as well as local, state and federal law enforcement agencies.

Essential Functions:

  • Provides department leadership to include directing shift activity in the absence of or in collaboration with the Supervisor and Lead Officers. Interprets policies and procedures, trains, equips and directs Public Safety personnel, and works towards positive resolution of internal and external customer issues.
  • Serves as a member of the department training program. Is engaged in the development and delivery of initial and ongoing training for Public Safety personnel, as well as participating in meetings associated with training development, coordination and delivery.
  • Answers hospital emergency line, intercom and elevator calls for assistance promptly and professionally. Operates various cameras and alarm systems. Performs parking enforcement related duties, to include, but not limited to, operating parking equipment, greeting, welcoming and directing customers.
  • Patrols (by foot or vehicle) assigned areas of facilities and grounds according to established schedule and investigates unusual occurrences. Performs security inspection tours and notifies appropriate personnel of problems, as necessary. Questions or detains suspicious individuals or criminal violators on hospital grounds. Restrains disorderly, combative or injurious individuals according to established training standards as necessary to prevent harm to self or others
  • Investigates and documents incident reports on a wide variety of Public Safety-related incidents including but not limited to; crimes committed on the property, injuries sustained on the property, actual or potential loss of hospital, employee, patient, or visitor property through fire, theft, damage, or vandalism. Obtains evidence related to the incident and interviews victims, witnesses, and suspects. Processes/secures property and/or evidence as directed.
  • Responds to emergency situations of various types. Responses may include activities such as crowd control, disturbance resolution, verbal and physical intervention, firefighting duties, medical and other activities of a similar nature, including subsequent appearances in court, hearings, or chambers, as requested.
  • Performs Weapon Screening services at designated locations to prevent weapons and other prohibited property from entering Children's facilities. Secures property/weapons as needed and/or directed. Liaison with MRMC Campus Public Safety/Security departments, as well as, local, state and federal law enforcement agencies.
  • Badges and screens visitors against visitation policy using skills obtained through training and/or work experience. Determines guest's destination and/or transportation needs. Provides precise way finding. Directs and/or escorts employees, visitors, clients, and patients as well as vehicle traffic to all areas of hospital, clinic, grounds, facilities, etc. Performs traffic control functions as needed.
  • Provides basic hospital information services, as needed, including being assigned to a Welcome Center.
  • Performs special assignments and projects as directed. Performs other related Public Safety, general office or record keeping tasks.

Experience:

  • Strong interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills are necessary in order to effectively interact with a variety of hospital employees, staff and visitors, sometimes under potentially stressful situations.

title: Head of Strategic Projects
description:
Job Family Group:

Retail Group


Job Description:

At bp, we provide an excellent working environment and employee benefits such as an open and inclusive culture, a great work-life balance, tremendous learning and development opportunities to craft your career path, life and health insurance, medical care package and many others.

Are you passionate about turning strategy into tangible results?

We are seeking a Head of Strategic Projects to lead bp's Mobility & Convenience Americas (M&CA) strategy and transformation portfolio, driving the execution of strategic, operational, and digital initiatives that accelerate growth, enhance customer experiences, and improve business performance.

This is a senior leadership role for someone who pairs the structured problem-solving difficulty of a premier strategy house with deep delivery instinct and operational leadership experience: owning transformation roadmaps, driving enterprise-wide business change, leading agile, product-based delivery at pace, and being accountable for measurable business outcomes. You will lead a team and set the delivery standard across strategic, operational, and digital transformation programs.

Core accountabilities (shared across the leadership team)

  • Strategy to execution: Translate enterprise and Customers-level strategy into clear, actionable roadmaps with landmarks, critical metrics, and success measures. Drive execution across strategic, operational, and digital priorities, ensuring delivery of measurable business outcomes.
  • Portfolio leadership & accountability: lead a portfolio of high-impact initiatives; handle interdependencies and risk, and be accountable for on-time delivery of outcomes and value.
  • Insight & decision leadership: Direct advanced analyses, financial modeling, value assessment, benchmarking, and operational performance reviews, and make the calls, turning complex data into decisions for senior leaders.
  • Executive narrative ownership: author and present compelling narratives for governance forums, performance reviews, and board-level updates; chair governance where you lead the agenda.
  • Team leadership & capability building: Lead, mentor, and grow a high-performing team. Build organizational capability across transformation, strategy execution, operational improvement, and digital delivery.

What sets this role apart

  • Be responsible for the transformation delivery strategy: Define and lead the transformation delivery strategy for M&CA across strategy, operations, and digital initiatives, and prioritize the portfolio to enhance business value.
  • Enable products, platforms & business transformation: Partner with Technology, Product, Engineering, Customers, and Operations to deliver scalable digital products and platforms while driving broader business transformation and performance improvement initiatives.
  • Drive operational excellence: Partner with business leaders to improve operational performance, simplify processes, strengthen governance, and embed continuous improvement across the organization. Lead initiatives that enhance organizational effectiveness and sustainable business performance.
  • Set delivery excellence: Establish and continuously improve agile delivery frameworks, governance, tools, and metrics across squads and transformation programs. Ensure consistent execution standards across strategic, operational, and digital initiatives.
  • Own value realization: Ensure transformation initiatives deliver measurable outcomes, revenue growth, cost efficiency, customer impact, and operational improvements, and track benefits realization.

What you will need to be successful

We are looking for an exceptional problem-solver with a strong delivery instinct, operational leadership capability, and the seniority to lead. For this role, we require deep experience leading large-scale transformation initiatives across strategy, operations, and digital delivery, with a consistent track record to translate strategy into execution and measurable business outcomes.

Experience (tiered)

  • Essential: 15+ years of post-university experience, including team leadership, with a strong foundation in best-in-class management consulting, McKinsey, BCG, or Bain. Significant experience leading sophisticated, cross-functional transformation portfolios spanning strategy, operations, and digital delivery.
  • Strongly preferred: Subsequent experience in oil & gas, ideally downstream (fuels, retail fuels, convenience, mobility).
  • Nice to have: Hands-on experience in retail and/or convenience. Experience working within agile product organizations and digital transformation environments.
  • Education: Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience or relevant professional qualification (MBA beneficial but not required).

Key skills

  • Structured thinking & judgment: frame sophisticated problems, test hypotheses, and make sound, data-driven decisions under ambiguity.
  • Advanced analytics: strong quantitative and qualitative skills — financial modeling, market assessment, scenario analysis, and clear synthesis.
